title: Settings Screen
content: #contentsRT System EditorThis section explains the settings screen of RT System Editor.The RT System Editor settings screen can be displayed from the menu by selecting [window] > [preferences] > [RT System Editor].&aname(cycle);ConnectionIn the connection settings, you configure the heartbeat settings for the state notification observer and the connection cycle settings.In middleware that supports the state notification observer (OpenRTM-aist 1.1 or later), RTC liveness is checked by sending heartbeats to the observer. The heartbeat setting items are as follows.Heartbeat Setting Items      Name    Description        Enable heartbeat    Specifies whether to enable timeout detection by heartbeat.        Heartbeat receive interval    Specifies the heartbeat receive interval.The unit is seconds, and the default is 1.0 second.        Heartbeat receive count    Specifies the number of heartbeat receptions for timeout detection.Receive interval x receive count = timeout time [seconds]The default is 3 times.  The connection cycle is the cycle at which the System Editor collects system information and reflects it in the display in conventional middleware (OpenRTM-aist 1.0 or earlier).The unit is milliseconds. If 0 is specified, synchronization is not performed.Connection Cycle Settings Screen&aname(color);Display ColorOn the display color settings screen, you can set the colors of the RTC and ExecutionContext states displayed in the System Editor.For the meaning of each state, see RTC Display in the System Editor.Display Color Settings Screen&aname(icon);IconOn the icon settings screen, you can set the icon image assigned to RTCs displayed in the System Editor and the display target pattern.For the display target, set a pattern for the RTC type or category.For an example of icon image display, see RTC Display in the System Editor.Icon Image Settings ScreenUse the [Add], [Edit], and [Delete] buttons to add, edit, or delete icon image entries.Clicking the [Add] or [Edit] button opens the icon image settings dialog, where you set the display target pattern and icon image file.Icon Image Settings ScreenAfter setting the display pattern, click the [Apply] or [OK] button to apply the settings.Clicking the [Import] or [Export] button allows you to load the list of icon image settings from an XML file or save it to an XML file.&aname(offline);Offline EditorYou can set the parameters that can be selected when connecting ports in the Offline Editor.The configurable items are [Interface Type], [Data Flow Type], and [Subscription Type]. When connecting ports, you can select values from the parameters set here.For the meaning of each item, see data port connections.Offline Settings Screen&aname(online);Online EditorIn the Online Editor, you can set whether to perform confirmation before executing RTC actions.The default value is unchecked (confirmation is not performed).Online Settings ScreenRT Name Service View&aname(ns-conn);Connection CycleThe connection cycle is the cycle at which RT Name Service View collects system information and reflects it in the display.&brThere are two connection cycles: one for the Name Service View and one for the System Editor. The unit is milliseconds. If 0 is specified, synchronization is not performed.Connection Cycle Settings Screen&aname(ns-sync);SynchronizationThe timeout wait time is the amount of time to wait when a connection to the system cannot be established while collecting system information (unit: milliseconds).Connection Cycle Settings ScreenThe relationship between the connection cycle and the synchronization timeout wait time is shown below.(Example: connection cycle is 1000 ms, synchronization timeout wait time is 100 ms)Relationship Between Connection Cycle and Synchronization Timeout Wait Time

title: Views (Overview)
content: #contentsRTSystemEditor uses the following views.Views of RT System EditorList of Views      No.    View Name    Description        1    Name Service View    Displays the contents of the name service where RTCs are registered in a tree format.        2    Configuration View    Displays and edits the configuration information of the selected RTC.        3    Manager Control View    Controls the selected manager.        4    Composite Component View    Displays and sets the port public information of the selected composite RTC.        5    Execution Context View    Displays a list of execution contexts (ECs) to which the selected RTC belongs, executes RTC and EC actions, and attaches/detaches RTCs to/from ECs.        6    Log View    Displays log messages notified by the log notification observer.        7    Property View    Displays the profile information of the selected RTC.        8    System Editor    Displays RTCs graphically and creates RT systems.        9    Offline System Editor    Graphically displays the contents of the RT Repository and local RT component specification files, and creates RT systems.  The following sections explain each view.

title: System Editor (Composite Components)
content: #contentsThis section explains how to operate composite components.Creating a Composite ComponentYou can combine multiple components into a composite component.Select the components you want to make into a composite component, right-click them, and select “Create Composite Component”. The composite component creation dialog will be displayed.Creating a Composite ComponentComposite Component Creation DialogThe items in the dialog are as follows.Dialog Items and Requirements for Creating a Composite Component      No.    Dialog Description    Description        ①    Manager    Select a manager from the list of managers displayed in the Name Service View. The manager selected here creates the composite component.        ②    Name    Specifies the instance name of the composite component.        ③    Type    Specifies the type of composite component. The available types are as follows.[PeriodicECShared]Each RTC operates by sharing only the ExecutionContext. Since the state of each RTC is independent, multiple states may exist within the composite component.[PeriodicStateShared]Each RTC operates by sharing the same ExecutionContext as well as the same state.[Grouping]A composite component in which each RTC shares nothing, and each RTC maintains its own ExecutionContext and state.        ④    Path    Specifies the path to be set for the composite component.        ⑤    Port    Selects the ports to be displayed on the composite component from the list of ports of the child components.Proxy ports are created on the composite component for the ports selected here.        ⑥    -    Buttons for selecting all ports and clearing all port selections  When a composite component is created, the components that were selected as child components disappear from the System Editor, and the new composite component is drawn.Double-click the composite component diagram, or right-click it and select “Open in Editor”. A new System Diagram opens and the inside of the composite component is displayed.Opening a Composite Component in the System EditorSystem Editor Displaying the Inside of a Composite Component  However, when saving the system configuration, drawing information for a component can be saved only once for each component, so drawing information changed in the System Diagram that displays the inside of the composite component is not saved.Adding a Child to a Composite ComponentOpen the System Editor that displays the inside of the composite component, and drag and drop an RTC from the Name Service View. This adds the RTC as a child of the composite component. All ports of the added child RTC are set to private.Adding a Child RTCDeleting a Child from a Composite ComponentOpen the System Editor that displays the inside of the composite component, and delete the child component there. This deletes the child from the composite component.The deleted child component disappears from inside the composite component and is displayed in the original System Diagram (the diagram in which the composite component itself is displayed).Deleting a Child Component from Inside a Composite ComponentDisplaying a Child Component on the System Editor Where the Composite Component Is DisplayedDeleting a Composite ComponentRight-click the composite component and select “Delete”. The composite component is deleted from the diagram.If the composite component is open in another System Diagram when it is deleted, a dialog confirming that the editor should be closed is displayed.Deleting a Composite ComponentDialog Confirming Closure of the Editor Displaying the Composite ComponentDecomposing a Composite ComponentRight-click the composite component and select “Decompose Composite Component”. This sends exist() to the composite component and terminates the component itself.If the composite component is open in another System Diagram when it is decomposed, a dialog confirming that the editor should be closed is displayed.When the composite component is decomposed, the child components are displayed in the original System Diagram (the diagram where the composite component was displayed).Decomposing a Composite ComponentDialog Confirming Closure of the Editor Displaying the Composite ComponentSwitching Ports Between Public and PrivateIf the ports of a component in the System Editor that displays the inside of the composite component are exposed on the composite component, they are displayed with different icons as shown below.Icons for Public Ports of Child RTCs      No.    Name    Shape        1    InPort            2    OutPort            3    ServicePort      Right-click a public port and select “Unexport” to change the port to a non-public state. Also, right-click a non-public port and select “Export” to change the port to a public state.            Public/Private Port SettingHowever, if the port is connected to a port of another component, it cannot be set to “Unexport”.When There Is a Port Connection

title: Installation and Startup
content: #contentsThis section explains how to install and start RTSystemEditor.Installing RTSystemEditorSince RTSystemEditor is an Eclipse plugin, you must first install Eclipse itself and the other Eclipse plugins it depends on.For installation, see Installing OpenRTM Eclipse tools.Starting RTSystemEditor  When you start Eclipse for the first time after installation, a “Welcome” screen like the following is displayed.Click “✖” at the upper left of the screen to close the “Welcome” screen.  On the following screen, click the [Open Perspective] button at the upper right.  Select [RT System Editor] and click the [OK] button.  RTSystemEditor starts.

title: Views (Composite Component View)
content: This section explains the Composite Component View.Location of the Composite Component ViewIn the Composite Component View, port public/private information for the selected composite RTC is displayed, and you can set ports to public or private.Composite Component ViewScreen Layout of the Composite Component View      No.    Description        ①    Instance name of the composite RTC.        ②    Type name of the composite RTC.        ③    Public/private state of the port.        ④    Instance name of the child RTC included in the composite RTC.        ⑤    Port name of the child RTC included in the composite RTC.        ⑥    Applies changes to the public/private state of ports.        ⑦    Cancels changes to the public/private state of ports.  Information being edited in the Composite Component View is not applied until the [Apply] button in ⑥ is clicked. Information being modified (not yet applied) is displayed in light red. Ports selected in the System Editor are displayed in light yellow.Editing Port Public/Private SettingsPort Selected in the System EditorIf a port of a composite component is connected to a port of another component, the corresponding port is displayed in gray in the Composite Component View and cannot be edited.When Connected to Another Port

title: System Editor (Save)
content: #contentsThis section explains how to save and open the System Editor.Saving the System EditorThe System Editor can be saved. To save it, select [File] from the menu or right-click the editor and select “Save”. (“Save As…” allows you to freely select the file to save.)          System Editor Save Menu    Context Menu  When you select system save, the profile information dialog opens. Set the required items and click the [OK] button to save the system information to a file.Profile Information DialogProfile Information Items      Name    Shape        Vendor    Vendor name. An element that makes up the RT system identifier.Required item.        System Name    System name. An element that makes up the RT system identifier.Required item.        Version    System version. An element that makes up the RT system identifier.Required item.        Path    File name used to save the system.Required item.        Update Log    Describes supplementary information such as version notes.        Required    Check the RTCs required to operate the RT system.  Opening a Saved System EditorTo open a saved System Editor, right-click the editor and select “Open”.Opening the System EditorAfter opening, RT System Editor treats the remote system as the correct source and updates it with the latest information. To restore the saved contents to the system, use “Open and Restore…”, described in the next section.Opening and Restoring a Saved SystemTo open and restore a saved System Editor, right-click the editor and select “Open and Restore…” or “Open and Quick Restore…”.Opening and Restoring the System EditorThe following contents are restored to the system.  Connections between ports (when the connector from the time of saving does not exist)  Configuration information~During restoration, the name service is searched using the component path ID to obtain the remote component.When “Quick Restore” is selected, before accessing the name service, it attempts to obtain the remote component using the IOR saved in the profile. If it cannot be obtained, the name service is searched.If restoration fails, the error details are displayed.Error Message for Restoration FailureRT System Editor also attempts to restore as much as possible even when an error occurs.

title: Views (Manager Control View)
content: This section explains the Manager Control View.Location of the Manager Control ViewWhen a manager is selected in the Name Service View, the Manager Control View becomes active, and the selected manager can be controlled.Manager Control ViewScreen Layout of the Manager Control View      No.    Description        ①    Button for displaying the list of loadable modules.        ②    Button for displaying the list of loaded modules.        ③    Button for displaying the component list.        ④    Component creation button.Opens the component creation dialog and creates a new component. The created component is displayed in the component list display in ③.        ⑤    Manager duplication button. Starts a new manager. * Currently unavailable because the specification has not yet been determined.        ⑥    Manager termination button. Terminates the selected manager. * Currently unavailable because the specification has not yet been determined.        ⑦    Table that displays lists of modules and components.        ⑧    Specifies the URL when loading a module by specifying a URL.        ⑨    Module load and unload buttons.Loads or unloads the module selected in the table in ⑦, or the module specified by URL.  To load a module into the manager, click the [Loadable Modules] button. When you select a displayed loadable module, the [Load] button becomes enabled, and clicking it loads the module.You can also add a module by specifying a URL by entering the module URL in the “URL:” text box and clicking the [Load] button.Loading a ModuleTo unload a module, click the [Loaded Modules] button. When you select a displayed loaded module, the [Unload] button becomes enabled, and clicking it unloads the module.Unloading a ModuleTo create a new component, click the [Create] button to open the component creation dialog, select the type of component to create, and click [OK]. The component is then created.The created component is registered with the name service by the manager and appears in the component list displayed by the [Active Components] button.Component Creation DialogThe component type is selected from the components defined in modules already loaded into the manager.In Parameter, component creation parameters can be specified in the format “param1=value1&param2=value2”. The following common parameters can be set for all components.Common Parameters for Component Creation      Parameter Name    Description        instance_name    Instance name of the component.If not specified, a serial number is appended to the component type (type_name).        type_name    Component type        description    Component description        version    Component version        vendor    Component provider        category    Component category  You can also specify ConfigurationSet values using component creation parameters.ConfigurationSet parameters are specified in the format “conf.NNNN.PPPP=VVVV”, where NNNN is the ConfigurationSet name, PPPP is the parameter name, and VVVV is the setting value.For example, to create a ConsoleIn component, create a ConfigurationSet named mode1, and specify the parameters input_mode and input_cycle, the settings are as follows.Specifying ConfigurationSet Parameters When Creating a ComponentIn addition, arbitrary parameters can be specified depending on the component.

title: Views (Configuration View)
content: This section explains the Configuration View.Location of the Configuration ViewIn the Configuration View, you can display and edit the configuration of the selected RTC. The list of CofigurationSets is displayed on the left, and the properties in the ConfigurationSet are displayed on the right.Configuration ViewScreen Layout of the Configuration View      No.    Description        ①    Name of the selected component.        ②    Name of the selected ConfigurationSet.        ③    The active ConfigurationSet. The active ConfigurationSet can also be changed.        ④    List of ConfigurationSets.        ⑤    Name of the property of the ConfigurationSet selected on the left.        ⑥    Value of the property of the ConfigurationSet selected on the left.        ⑦    Buttons for adding/deleting ConfigurationSets.        ⑧    Buttons for adding/deleting properties.        ⑨    Button for opening the settings value edit dialog, and buttons for applying/canceling changes.  Information being edited in the Configuration View is not applied until the [Apply] button in ⑨ is clicked. Information being modified (not yet applied) is displayed in red.Configuration View During ModificationTo edit configuration settings values, click the [Edit] button in ⑨ to open the edit dialog and perform the editing.Configuration Edit DialogIf there are multiple ConfigurationSets, you can switch the target to edit using the tabs (⑩) at the top of the dialog.For each configuration parameter, you can specify a widget for editing. If a widget type is defined in the ConfigurationSet, the parameter can be edited with the specified widget (⑪).Widget types include slider, spinner, radio button, checkbox, and ordered list. If no widget type is specified, a text box is used by default.Constraints can also be specified for each parameter. If the widget type is slider or spinner, specifying constraints is required. If the corresponding widget type is defined but no constraints are specified, the default text box is used.List of Widget Types      Widget Type    Image    Description        Slider        Select a value within the range from the minimum value to the maximum value specified by the constraints using the slider. Input in the text box is also possible.        Spinner        Select a value within the range from the minimum value to the maximum value specified by the constraints using the spinner. Decimal precision follows the notation of the minimum and maximum values in the constraints. However, negative values cannot be specified.Example: If the maximum value is "10.00", two decimal places are used.        Radio Button        Select a value with radio buttons.        Checkbox        Select values with checkboxes. Multiple values can be selected and are set as comma-separated values.      Ordered List        Select values from the selection list on the left. Multiple values can be selected, the order is preserved, and duplicates are allowed. The selected values are set as comma-separated values, as with checkboxes.        Text Box        Set using normal text input.  </table>If constraints are specified for each parameter, the input value is checked against the constraints, and if the conditions are not satisfied, the form is shown in red.Also, when editing is confirmed with the [OK] button, constraint checks are performed for all parameters of the ConfigurationSet that have been changed, and if any parameter does not satisfy the constraints, an error dialog is displayed.Constraint Check Error DisplayWhile the [Apply] checkbox (⑫) in the configuration edit dialog is checked, changes to settings values are reflected in real time in the RTC.The information displayed in the Configuration View is cached and displayed with the latest information when the RTC is selected (to prepare for editing the configuration).Therefore, if the same RTC remains selected for a long time, differences from the system information may occur. Please note that when applying edits, RT System Editor completely overwrites the system with the edited information as the correct information, without considering these differences.Also, according to the RTC specification, any object can be registered as the Value of a property, but only strings can be registered/edited from RT System Editor.

title: System Editor (Connecting Ports)
content: #contentsThis section explains connections between data ports and between service ports.Data Port ConnectionsFor data port connections, connect an “InPort” and an “OutPort”. When you connect them by drag and drop, the following dialog is displayed. Note that the “Buffer” setting items are hidden when the dialog is initially displayed.Data Port Connector Profile DialogThe dialog items and conditions are as follows.Dialog Items and Requirements for Data Port Connections      No.    Dialog Item Name    ConnectorProfile    Requirements        ①    Name    name    None in particular        ②    Data Type    <<properties>>dataport.data_type    Specifies the data type to be sent and received between the data ports connected by this connector.Select from the data types that each port can send and receive to and from the other port. However, if Any is included, any value from the other port is accepted.        ③    Instance Type    <<properties>>dataport.interface_type    Specifies the interface type assumed by the RT system designer or supported by the RT middleware on which the RTC operates.Select from the interface types supported by both ports. However, if Any is included, any interface from the other port is accepted.        ④    Dataflow Type    <<properties>>dataport.dataflow_type    Specifies the dataflow type assumed by the RT system designer or supported by the RT middleware on which the RTC operates.Select from the dataflow types supported by both ports. However, if Any is included, any dataflow from the other port is accepted.        ⑤    Subscription Type    <<properties>>dataport.subscription_type    [Requirement when the value of Dataflow Type is Push]Specifies the subscription type assumed by the RT system designer or supported by the RT middleware on which the RTC operates.Select from the subscription types supported by both ports. However, if Any is included, any subscription type from the other port is accepted.        ⑥    Push Rate(Hz)    <<properties>>dataport.push_interval    [Requirement when the value of Dataflow Type is "Push" and Subscription Type is "Periodic"]Specifies the data transmission cycle when the subscription type is "Periodic". Specify the transmission cycle as a positive numeric value (decimals allowed).        ⑦    Push Policy    <<properties>>dataport.publisher.push_policy    Data transmission policy. [Requirement when the value of Dataflow Type is "Push" and Subscription Type is "Periodic"] Select from all, fifo, skip, and new.all: Sends all data in the buffer at oncefifo: Sends data in the buffer one item at a time in FIFO orderskip: Sends data while skipping data in the buffernew: Sends the latest value in the buffer (old values are discarded).        ⑧    Skip Count    <<properties>>dataport.publisher.skip_count    Number of transmission data items to skip. [Requirement when the value of Push Policy is "skip"] Data in the buffer is thinned out and sent according to this setting value.        ⑨    Details    ―    When the checkbox is checked, detailed setting items for the input/output port buffers are displayed.They are hidden when the dialog is initially displayed.        ⑩⑮    Buffer length(OutPort/InPort)    <<properties>>buffer.length    Buffer length        ⑪⑯    Buffer full policy(OutPort/InPort)    <<properties>>buffer.write.full_policy    Behavior when the buffer is full during data writing to the buffer. Select from overwrite, do_nothing, and block.overwrite: Overwrites the data.do_nothing: Does nothing.block: Blocks.If block is specified, and the following timeout value is specified, a timeout occurs if writing is not possible after the specified time. The default is overwrite.        ⑫⑰    Buffer write timeout(OutPort/InPort)    <<properties>>buffer.write.timeout    The time until a timeout event is generated when writing data to the buffer (unit: seconds)The default is 1.0 [sec]. If 0.0 is set, no timeout occurs.        ⑬⑱    Buffer empty policy(OutPort/InPort)    <<properties>>buffer.read.empty_policy    Behavior when the buffer is empty during data reading from the buffer. Select from readblock, do_nothing, and block.readblock: Re-reads the last element.do_nothing: Does nothing.block: Blocks.If block is specified, and the following timeout value is specified, a timeout occurs if reading is not possible after the specified time. The default is readback.        ⑭⑲    Buffer read timeout(OutPort/InPort)    <<properties>>buffer.read.timeout    The time until a timeout event is generated when reading data from the buffer (unit: seconds)The default is 1.0 [sec]. If 0.0 is set, no timeout occurs.        ⑳21    Name/Value    <<properties>>Name    Sets arbitrary propertiesItems can be added with the [Add] button and deleted with the [Delete] button.The entered items are set in the Properties of the ConnectorProfile in NVList format.Properties with the same Key cannot be set.  For items ② through ⑤, RT System Editor creates the selectable values by matching strings from the value lists of each port.If only ANY is specified for both ports, it is not possible to determine the values that can be entered.For this reason, when ANY is included in both ports, RT System Editor allows arbitrary strings to be entered. Items for which arbitrary strings can be entered display “Arbitrary input allowed”.Display When Arbitrary Input Is AllowedService Port ConnectionsFor service port connections, connect a “ServicePort” and a “ServicePort”. When you connect them by drag and drop, the following dialog is displayed.Service Port Connector Profile DialogThe dialog items and conditions are as follows.Dialog Items and Requirements for Service Port Connections      No.    Dialog Item Name    ConnectorProfile    Requirements        ①    Name    Name    None in particular        ②    Details    ―    When the checkbox is checked, detailed setting items for Consumer/Provider are displayed.They are hidden when the dialog is initially displayed.        ③    Consumer    ―    Select from the list of Consumers of the interfaces set for the service ports to be connected.The selection list in the ComboBox is displayed in the format <component name>:<interface name>:<instance name>.The added Consumer/Provider pair is stored in the ConnectorProfile with the Consumer ID as the property key and the Provider ID as the property value.The Consumer/Provider IDs are represented in the following format.<rtc_name>.port.<port_name>.<if_polality>.<if_tname>.<if_iname>rtc_name is the component nameport_name is the port nameif_polality is "required" for Consumer and "provided" for Providerif_tname is the type name of the interfaceif_iname is the instance name of the interface        ④    Provider    <<properties>>Set with the Consumer ID as the key    As with Consumer, select from the list of Providers of the interfaces set for the service ports to be connected.        ⑤    Add    ―    Adds a new Consumer/Provider entry.        ⑥    Delete    ―    Deletes the selected Consumer/Provider entry.        ⑦⑧    Name/Value    <<properties>>Name    Sets arbitrary propertiesItems can be added with the [Add] button and deleted with the [Delete] button.The entered items are set in the Properties of the ConnectorProfile in NVList format.Properties with the same Key cannot be set.  For service ports, there are no required connection conditions. However, if the PortInterfaceProfiles between the ServicePorts do not match completely (*1), a warning is displayed in the connection dialog.Warning Display in the Service Port Connection Dialog*1A complete match here means that the “type” of the PortInterfaceProfiles is the same and that the “polarity” values are PROVIDED and REQUIred for each other.It also means that all PortInterfaceProfiles match without any excess (each port can have multiple PortInterfaceProfiles).

title: Offline System Editor
content: #contentsOverviewThis section explains the overview of the Offline System Editor.Location of the Offline System EditorIn the Offline System Editor, you edit an RT system by adding components from the Repository View to the diagram by drag and drop. The basic operations are the same as those of the online System Editor, but you cannot change the state of RTCs. Also, RTC states are not changed or updated in real time.Basic FunctionsOpening the Offline System EditorTo open a new Offline System Editor, click the “Open New Offline System Editor” button on the toolbar, or select [File] > [Open New Offline System Editor] from the menu bar.Open New Offline System Editor from the ToolbarOpen New Offline System Editor from the File MenuPlacing Component Specifications in the Offline System EditorTo place component specifications in the Offline System Editor, drag and drop the component specifications from the Repository View.Placing Component Specifications in the Offline System EditorIf you click component specifications in the Repository View while holding down the Ctrl key and select multiple component specifications, you can place them all together in the Offline System Editor.Placing Multiple Component Specifications Together in the Offline System EditorEditing Component Specifications in the Offline System EditorIn the Offline System Editor, you can perform most of the operations available in the System Editor, except for those related to the operation of runtime components, using the same operations as in the System Editor.Deployment FunctionThis section explains the overview of the deployment function using the Offline System Editor.By using the deployment function, you can build an actual system from an offline profile created in the Offline System Editor.Setting Deployment InformationRight-click a component placed in the Offline Editor and select “Set Deploy Info.” from the displayed menu. The deployment information settings screen is displayed.Setting Deployment Information                  Running RTCs    Running Managers  Deployment Information Settings ScreenThe deployment information settings screen displays a list of currently running RTCs and Managers. Select the element to use when deploying the target RTC.      The contents of the deployment information settings screen use the items displayed in NameServiceView. If information about running elements is not displayed, check the display contents of NameServiceView and refresh it as necessary.        If a composite RTC is selected, only the Manager information list is displayed. Select the Manager to use during deployment.  Saving and Loading Deployment InformationThe configured deployment information can be saved and loaded separately from the RtsProfile. Right-click the Offline Editor and select “Save Deploy Info.” or “Load Deploy Info.” from the displayed menu.Saving and Loading Deployment Information  When loading deployment information, the corresponding RTC is searched for using the component ID (vendor name, category name, component name, and version number) as the key.Executing DeploymentTo build (deploy) an actual system based on the configured deployment information, right-click the Offline Editor and select “Deploy System” from the displayed menu.DeploymentWhen deployment is executed, the actual system is built (deployed) based on the configured deployment information. Then, a new online editor is opened and the deployment result is displayed.If there is a component in the target offline system for which deployment information has not been configured, or if the configured deployment target is not running at the time of deployment, a warning screen like the following is displayed.Warning Screen During DeploymentIf “Cancel” is selected on the warning screen, the deployment process is aborted. If [OK] is selected, the system is built (deployed) as much as possible using the running deployment targets.

title: System Editor (RTC Display / Drawing Editing)
content: #contentsThis section explains operations for displaying RTCs and editing RTC drawings.&aname(RTCcolor);RTC DisplayRTCs placed in the System Editor are displayed as rectangles, and ports are displayed around those rectangles. Each state is also represented by color.Example of RTC DisplayThe list of icons and state colors is as follows.Component and Port Icons      No.    Name    Shape    State    Default Color (*)        1    RTC        CREATED        White        INACTIVE        Blue        ACTIVE        Light Green        ERROR    Red        UNKNOWN        lack        2    Execution Context (first one only)    (outer border line of the RTC rectangle)    RUNNING        Gray        STOPPED    Black        3    InPort        Not connected        Blue        Connected (one or more)        Light Green        4    OutPort        Not connected        Blue        Connected (one or more)        Light Green        5    ServicePort        Not connected        light Blue        Connected (one or more)        Cyan  ’* The colors of each state can be changed from Display Color on the settings screen.’You can also attach icon images according to the RTC type and category.Example of RTC Icon Image Display’* Icon images can be changed from Icon on the settings screen.’RTC SynchronizationThe state of RTCs placed in the System Editor is monitored, and the display is updated in real time.The monitoring methods include the state notification observer method (OpenRTM-aist 1.1 or later) and periodic checking by polling. Monitoring parameters can be changed in the connection settings screen.When placing an RTC in the System Editor, the middleware version is checked, and if observers are supported, an observer is registered with the RTC. If observers are not supported, the state is queried periodically.State Notification ObserverWhen an RTC is deleted from the System Editor, the observer is also unregistered.The contents notified by the state notification observer are as follows.Notification Contents of the State Notification Observer      Notification    Description        COMPONENT_PROFILE    Notifies when there is a change in the component profile of the RTC        RTC_STATUS    RTC stateNotifies the new state and the ID of the target EC        EC_STATUS    Execution context stateNotifies execution rate changes, EC start/stop, and RTC attach/detach        PORT_PROFILE    Port stateNotifies port addition/deletion and connection/disconnection of connections        CONFIGURATION    Configuration stateNotifies configuration addition/change/deletion and switching of the active configuration  In addition, a heartbeat is notified at regular intervals to confirm that the RTC is alive.If the heartbeat is not notified a certain number of times, the RTC is regarded as having terminated abnormally and is removed from the System Editor.RTC Drawing EditingThis section explains RTC drawing editing. (The term “drawing editing” is intentionally used instead of “editing” because the work described here edits the drawing and has no effect on the system.)  Changing the size and moving an RTC (no effect on the system)~To move an RTC, select the RTC and drag it. To change the size of an RTC, drag the handles that are displayed when the RTC is selected.Moving an RTC (left) and changing the size of an RTC (right)The position and size of the selected RTC are also displayed in the status bar.Status Bar  Rotating an RTC (no effect on the system)~Select the target component and click the right mouse button while holding down the Ctrl key to rotate it to a horizontal orientation. Click the right mouse button while holding down the Shift key to rotate it to a vertical orientation. By repeating the same operations, you can change it to the opposite horizontal orientation or the opposite vertical orientation, allowing operation in the up, down, left, and right directions.Rotated RTC  Deleting an RTC (no effect on the system)~To delete an RTC, select the RTC and click the [Delete] button, or select [Delete] from the context menu.Deleting an RTC  Moving a connection line between ports (no effect on the system)~To move a connection line, select the connection line and move the displayed handler. Vertical lines can be moved left and right, and horizontal lines can be moved up and down.Moving connection lines: vertical line (left) and horizontal line (right)

title: Views (Name Service View)
content: #contentsThis section explains the Name Service View.In OpenRTM-aist, a name service is used to manage and publish RTCs, and the Name Service View allows you to display and edit this information.Function OverviewThe Name Service View provides functions for graphically operating RTCs in real time. The list of provided functions is as follows.#clearFunction Overview List      No.    Function Name    Function Overview        1    Name Server Connection/Edit Function    Connects to a name server and displays the registered components in the Name Service View in a tree format.        2    Component Profile Display Function    Displays the profile information of the selected component in the Property View.  Starting the Name Service ViewSelect [Window] > [Show View] > [Name Service View] from the menu to display the Name Service View.Show ViewInitial Startup Screen of the Name Service ViewConnecting to a Name ServerTo connect to a name server, click the [Add Name Server] button at the top of the Name Service View, or select [Add Name Server] from the context menu.Connecting to a Name ServerIn the name server connection dialog, enter the IP address and port number. (If the port number is omitted, the port number configured on the settings screen is used. The default port number is port 2809.)Name Server Connection DialogNote: When Eclipse is started or restarted, it automatically connects to the last connected address. If none exists, it attempts to connect to port 2809 on localhost.Removing a Name Server from the ScreenTo remove a connected name server from the screen, right-click the name server and select [Remove from View].Removing a Name Server from the ScreenDisplaying the Contents of a Name ServerIf components are registered in the connected name server, the registered contents are displayed in a tree format as shown below.Name Service ViewThe meanings of the icons are as follows.List of Name Server Icons      No.    Icon     Type (KIND)     Name        1        host_cxt    Host context        2        mgr_cxt    Manager context        3        cate_cxt    Category context        4        mod_cxt    Module context        5        Other than the above    Folder (contexts other than the above)        6        None    RTC        7        None    Manager        8        None    Object (object other than RTC)        9        None    Zombie object that is registered in the name server but whose actual object cannot be accessed  The Name Service View constantly monitors each connected name server and synchronizes and updates the display. (The monitoring cycle can be changed in [[Connection Cycle:]] on the settings screen.)Also, when you want to explicitly reacquire the contents of a name server, perform an update. To perform an update, click the [Refresh] button at the top of the Name Service View, or select [Refresh] from the context menu.RefreshChanging the Display Range of the Name Service ViewThe Name Service View has a function for moving the display root position to prevent the operation range from becoming complicated as the number of RTCs increases.To move the display root, select the destination, then click the [Jump Next] button at the top of the Name Service View, or select [Jump Next] from the context menu.Changing the Display RootExample of Changing the Display RootAfter moving, you can return one level up with [Back]. You can also return to the top-level hierarchy with [Back to Home].Filtering the Display Contents of the Name Service ViewAs another way to prevent the operation range from becoming complicated as the number of RTCs increases, the Name Service View has a filter function that limits the types of entries displayed.To set a filter, click the [Set Filter] button at the top of the Name Service View.Filter InstructionIn the “Set Filter” dialog, select the types of entries to hide from the “Select elements to exclude from the view” field.Name Service Filter DialogIf you check the elements you want to exclude from the Name Service View display, they will no longer be displayed in the Name Service View.When “Naming Object Name” is enabled, objects that match the object name condition are hidden.For the object name condition, prefix match and partial match can be selected.Filtering by Object NameDeleting an Entry from the Name ServiceIn the Name Service View, you can delete naming object entries from the name service. To delete a naming object, click [Delete from Name Service] in the context menu.Deleting from the Name ServiceRegistering an Object in the Name ServiceIn the Name Service View, you can register an object entry in the name service.To register an object, select [Add Object] from the context menu of the context or object under which you want to add the object.Adding an ObjectAdd Object DialogIn the “Add Object” dialog, specify the object name (Name), type (Kind), and IOR.Registering a Context in the Name ServiceIn the Name Service View, you can register a context entry in the name service.To register a context, select [Add Context] from the context menu of the context under which you want to add the context.Adding a ContextAdd Context DialogIn the “Add Context” dialog, specify the context name (Name) and type (Kind).For type (Kind), select one of the following values.List of Context Types (kind)      No.    Type (Kind)    Name        1    host_cxt    Host context        2    mgr_cxt    Manager context        3    cate_cxt    Category context        4    mod_cxt    Module context        5    Enter something other than the above    Folder (contexts other than the above)  Deleting Zombie ObjectsThe Name Service View has a function for deleting zombie objects all at once. To delete all zombie objects, click the [Clear Zombies] button at the top of the Name Service View.Clear Zombies

title: Views (Execution Context View)
content: This section explains the Execution Context View.Location of the Execution Context ViewIn the Execution Context View, you can display a list of execution contexts (ECs) to which the selected RTC belongs, start/stop ECs, execute RTC actions, and attach/detach RTCs to/from ECs. You can also set the execution cycle of ECs.Execution Context ViewScreen Layout of the Execution Context View      No.    Description        ①    Instance name of the RTC.        ②    Displays a list of ECs to which the RTC belongs. ECs owned by the RTC are displayed as "owned*", and ECs in which the RTC only participates are displayed as "participate*".        ③    Execution rate of the EC selected in ②.        ④⑤    Displays the properties of the selected EC as a list of Name and Value.　id: EC ID. In online mode, context_handle is displayed as the ID.　kind: EC type (PERIODIC/EVENT_DRIVEN/OTHER)　state: EC state (RUNNING/STOPPING)　component_state: State of the selected RTC on the EC (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/ERROR)　owner: Instance name of the owner RTC of this EC　participants: Number of RTCs participating in this ECOther arbitrary properties set for the EC are also displayed.        ⑥    Applies the entered execution rate to the EC.        ⑦    Starts the selected EC. (Not available offline)        ⑧    Stops the selected EC. (Not available offline)        ⑨    Activates the state of the selected RTC on the selected EC. (Not available offline)        ⑩    Deactivates the state of the selected RTC on the selected EC. (Not available offline)        ⑪    Resets the state of the selected RTC on the selected EC. (Not available offline)        ⑫    Detaches the selected RTC from the selected EC.However, if the RTC itself is the owner of the EC, it cannot be detached.        ⑬    Opens the RTC selection dialog on the System Editor and attaches the selected RTC to the EC.  The value being edited for the execution rate is not applied until the [Apply] button in ⑥ is clicked. Information being modified (not yet applied) is displayed in light red. If the input value is invalid, it is displayed in red.Editing the Execution RateWhen the Execution Rate Setting Value Is InvalidIn the online editor, you can operate ECs and change the state of RTCs on those ECs.Click the [Start] button to start the EC, and the state property becomes “RUNNING”. Click the [Stop] button to stop the EC, and state becomes “STOPPING”.To change the state of an RTC on an EC, click the [Activate] or [Deactivate] button. When activated, the component_state property becomes “ACTIVE”, and when deactivated, component_state becomes “INACTIVE”.If an RTC enters the “ERROR” state for some reason, click the [Reset] button to recover it.EC Operations and RTC State ChangesAn RTC can be attached to multiple ECs.Select the EC to which you want to add the RTC, and click the [Attach] button. The RTC selection dialog opens. The selection dialog displays a list of RTCs in the System Editor.RTC Selection DialogWhen you select an RTC and click [OK], the RTC is added to the EC, and the newly added EC is added to the list of participate ECs for the added RTC.Attaching an RTC to an ECTo detach an EC, select the participate EC and click the [Detach] button.Detaching an RTC from an EC

title: Views (Repository View)
content: This section explains the Repository View.The Repository View has a function for loading RT component specification description files and displaying them in a tree view.Repository ViewLoading a FileThis section explains how to specify and display an RT component specification description file in the Repository View.Right-click inside the Repository View and select [Load from File] from the displayed context menu. A file selection dialog is displayed. Select the RT component specification description file to load into the Repository View.This dialog is filtered to display only xml files.Loading a FileWhen a local RT component specification description file is loaded, the top level displays the absolute path of the loaded RT component specification description file.The second level displays the value of the category attribute defined in the RT component specification description file.The third level displays the value described in the name attribute in the RT component specification description file and the RT component specification description file name.Loading a DirectoryThis section explains how to specify a directory containing RT component specification description files and load and display all files in the directory.Right-click in the Repository View and select [Load from Directory] from the displayed context menu. A directory selection dialog is displayed.Select the directory to load into the Repository View. RT component specification description files under the directory are loaded.Loading a DirectoryThe display method is the same as when loading a file.If a new RT component specification description file is added to a directory that has already been expanded and loading is performed again, only the added RT component specification description file is loaded.DeletionComponents in the Repository View can be deleted by right-clicking in the Repository View and selecting [Delete] from the context menu.[Delete] can be selected only when a path, category, or component is selected.Deleting a ComponentIf the path, which is the top level, is deleted, the lower-level categories and components are also deleted at the same time. Also, if a component at the third level is deleted and no other components exist, the entries are deleted recursively up to the top level.

title: Overview and System Construction Flow
content: #contents(3)Overview of OpenRTM-aist RT System EditorAt present, OMG is developing specifications for Robot Technology Components (hereafter RTCs), which improve the efficiency of robot development.As a common platform that implements and applies these RTC specifications, the Integrated Intelligence Research Group, Intelligent Systems Research Institute, National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), provides OpenRTM-aist.RTSystemEditor is one of the development tools included in OpenRTM-aist, and it provides functions for graphically operating RTCs in real time.Also, as its name suggests, it is created as a plugin for the Eclipse integrated development environment, and can be operated seamlessly with existing plugins on Eclipse.&aname(target);Target AudienceThis document is intended for those who already have basic knowledge of RTCs.For details about RTCs, refer to the documents from OMG or here.&aname(screen);Screen ExampleThis section shows an example screen of OpenRTM-aist RT System Editor (hereafter RTSystemEditor).Example Screen of RTSystemEditor&aname(kinou);Function OverviewRTSystemEditor provides functions for graphically operating RTCs in real time. The list of provided functions is as follows.#clearFunction Overview List      No.    Function Name    Function Overview        1    Component Configuration Display/Edit Function    Displays and edits the configuration profile information of the selected component in the Configuration View.        2    Component Operation Change Function    Changes the operation of the selected component.        3    RT System Assembly Function    Assembles a system on the System Editor.        4    System Save/Open Function    Saves the contents of the System Editor as an RTS profile. Opens an RTS profile in the System Editor. The system port connections and configuration are not changed.        5    System Restore Function    Opens an RTS profile in the System Editor and restores the system based on the contents of the profile. (Reconstructs the system port connections and configuration based on the contents of the profile.)  &aname(kankyou);Operating EnvironmentThe environment required for RTSystemEditor operation is as follows.Operating Environment      No.    Environment    Notes        1    Java Development Kit 6    Note: It does not work with Java 1.5 (5.0).;        2    Eclipse 3.4 or later    Eclipse itself        3    Eclipse EMF 2.4 or later (including SDO and XSD)    Eclipse plugin on which RTSystemEditor depends * Use a version that matches the version of Eclipse you are using.        4    Eclipse GEF 3.4 or later    Eclipse plugin on which RTSystemEditor depends * Use a version that matches the version of Eclipse you are using.        5    RT Name Service View    Development tool included in OpenRTM-aist on which RTSystemEditor depends        6    RT Repository View    Development tool included in OpenRTM-aist on which RTSystemEditor depends  RestrictionsRTSystemEditor was developed for OpenRTM-aist. Operations for other RTC platforms are not assumed.

title: Views (Property View)
content: This section explains the Property View.Location of the Property ViewThe Property View displays profile information of RTCs and connectors selected in the System Dialog in real time. (Even while an RTC is selected, if a change is detected, it is reflected immediately.)      For RTC    For Composite RTC    For Manager                  Property ViewThe meanings of the displayed icons are as follows.List of Property Icons      No.    Icon    Name    Display Contents        1        RTC    InstanceName, TypeName, Description, Vender, Category, State (*displayed based on the LifeCycleState of the first ExecutionContext)        2        ExecutionContext    State, Kind, Rate        3        ServicePort    Name, list of property information        4        Outport    Name, list of property information        5        Inport    Name, list of property information        6        PortInterfaceProfile    InterfaceName, TypeName, PortInterfacePolarity        7        Manager    Components (list of created component names)Loadable Modules (list of loadable module names)Loaded Modules (list of loaded module names)  According to the RTC specification, an RTC’s LifeCycleState exists for each ExecutionContext. Therefore, multiple states exist, but RT System Editor displays STATE using only the first ExecutionContext.

title: System Editor (Basic Operations)
content: #contentsThis section explains the overview and basic operations of the System Editor.OverviewIn the System Editor, the state of RTCs is displayed in real time. You can also build systems and verify operation by connecting ports and changing the state of RTCs.#clear                  System Editor Location    System Editor  Basic OperationsThis section explains how to connect ports between RTCs and how to execute RTCs.Opening the System EditorTo open a new System Editor, click the [Open New System Editor] button on the toolbar, or select [File] > [Open New System Editor] from the menu bar.Open New System Editor from the ToolbarOpen New System Editor from the File MenuPlacing an RTC in the System EditorTo place an RTC in the System Editor, drag and drop the RTC from the Name Service View.Placing an RTC in the System EditorIf you click RTCs in the name service while holding down the [Ctrl] key and select multiple RTCs, you can place them all together in the System Editor.Placing Multiple RTCs Together in the System EditorNote that RTCs that have already been placed in the System Editor, or parent RTCs and child RTCs of a composite RTC, cannot be added redundantly.When placing multiple RTCs, duplicate RTCs are skipped, and when placing a single RTC, an error dialog is displayed.Duplicate RTC Placement Error DialogChanging the State of an RTCThis section explains how to change the state of an RTC.In the System Diagram, you can select an RTC and execute “Activate”, “Deactivate”, “Reset”, “Finalize”, “Exit”, “Start”, and “Stop”.You can also execute them in the same way from the Name Service View.            Changing the RTC State from the Name Service View (left) and the System Editor (right)The meanings of these actions are as follows. Please pay attention to the execution target.Actions for Changing the RTC State      No.    Action Name    Execution Target    Meaning        1    Activate    Executed for the selected RTC and its first ExecutionContext    Requests Activate        2    Deactivate    〃    Requests Deactivate        3    Reset    〃    Requests Reset        4    Exit    Executed for the selected RTC    Requests Exit        5    Start    Executed for the first ExecutionContext of the selected RTC    Requests Start        6    Stop    〃    Requests Activate  If confirmation of action execution is enabled in the online editor item of “Settings Screen”, a confirmation dialog is displayed before the action is executed.Action Execution Confirmation DialogBy default, advance confirmation is disabled.Shortcut keys are assigned to Activate and Deactivate. By default, they are set as follows.・Activate → Ctrl + Alt + A ・Deactivate → Ctrl + Alt + D To change the key bindings, use “General” → “Keys” in the standard Eclipse settings menu.Also, as a function for easily operating the system, you can request Activate, Deactivate, Start, Stop, and changes for all RTCs included in the System Editor from the toolbar and context menu.All Execution (Toolbar, from left: All Activate, All Deactivate, All Start, All Stop)All-type actions are also performed for ExecutionContexts other than the first one. Please note that the results differ from activating or starting each RTC on the screen one by one.Connecting PortsIn the System Editor, you can connect RTC ports to each other.To connect ports, drag and drop one port to another port.Port ConnectionAfter the drag and drop is completed, a dialog prompting you to enter the information required for connection is displayed.Example of the ConnectorProfile DialogIn this dialog, a ConnectorProfile is created. The ConnectorProfile must be created so that the conditions required by each port are satisfied. This dialog prompts you with pull-down menus so that only values satisfying the required conditions can be entered.For a connection that cannot satisfy the required conditions, a prohibited mark is displayed during the drag-and-drop connection, and drag and drop cannot be performed.Connection Prohibited MarkPort connections are broadly divided into data port connections and service port connections. For details, please refer to “System Editor (Connecting Ports)”.Disconnecting a Port ConnectionTo disconnect a port connection, select the connection and click the [Delete] button, or click [Delete] displayed in the context menu.Deleting a ConnectionDisconnecting All Port ConnectionsTo disconnect all port connections, select a port, right-click it, and execute “All Disconnect”.Disconnecting All ConnectionsSetting a Single Port ConnectionYou can set a ConnectorProfile for a single port connection.Right-click a port and select “Connect” from the context menu. The ConnectorProfile settings dialog opens in the same way as for a port-to-port connection.Single Port ConnectionTo delete a single port connection, similarly select “Disconnect” from the right-click context menu and operate from the port disconnection dialog.Delete the target from the list of ConnectorProfiles displayed in the dialog, and click the [OK] button to perform the disconnection process.Port DisconnectionPort Disconnection DialogThe port disconnection dialog displays a list of all ConnectorProfiles for single port connections and normal port-to-port connections, so it can also be used to check single port connections that are not drawn in the diagram.Collecting LogsWith the log notification observer, RTC log messages can be collected by the tool. (OpenRTM-aist 1.1 or later)Right-click an RTC on the diagram and select “Start Logging” from the context menu to start log collection.For an RTC that has already started log collection, the menu display changes to “Stop Logging”, and log collection is stopped.For an RTC that does not support observers, the menu is disabled.      Starting Log Collection    Stopping Log Collection      Starting/Stopping Log CollectionFor log collection, as with the state notification observer, a reference to the log notification observer is registered with the RTC and notifications are received.The observer is registered when log collection is started from the context menu, and the observer is unregistered when log collection is stopped.Also, as with the state notification observer, the observer is unregistered when an RTC is removed from the diagram.In log notification, a data structure including the time and log level (log record) is sent from the RTC, and the tool accumulates the log data.The accumulated logs can be viewed using the Log View.Log Notification Observer

title: Views (Log View)
content: This section explains the Log View.Location of the Log ViewThe Log View displays a list of RTCs targeted for log collection on the selected diagram, and displays log messages notified from the RTCs.You can select the RTCs you want to display, and you can also filter the display by log level.Log ViewScreen Layout of the Log View      No.    Description        ①    Displays a list of RTCs in the selected diagram that are targeted for log collection.Logs of RTCs checked here are displayed.        ②    Specifies the threshold of the log level to display.Log messages at or above the specified level are displayed.        ③    Displays log messages. The display is filtered by RTC selection and log level specification.The displayed items are as follows.・Timestamp・Log level (SILENT/ERROR/WARN/INFO/DEBUG/TRACE/VERBOSE/PARANOID)・RTC instance name・Log notification target・Log message  When a diagram is selected, the list of RTCs targeted for log collection on the diagram is displayed in ①. Logs are notified from RTCs by the log notification observer function, and RTCs for which observers have been registered become targets for log collection.When you select (check) the RTCs whose logs you want to display from the list, messages are displayed in the log display table in ③.Log messages can also be filtered by log level. When you select the threshold level from the combo box in ②, only logs at or above the selected level are displayed. For example, if “INFO” is selected in the combo box, only “ERROR”, “WARN”, and “INFO” messages are displayed.Filtering the Log Display

title: RTSystemEditor-1.2.0
content: What Is RTSystemEditor?OMG is currently developing specifications for Robot Technology Components (hereafter RTCs), which improve the efficiency of robot development.As a common platform that implements and applies this RTC specification, the Task Intelligence Research Group, Intelligent Systems Research Institute, National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), provides OpenRTM-aist.RTSystemEditor is one of the development tools included in OpenRTM-aist, and it provides functions for graphically operating RTCs in real time.It is also created as a plugin for the Eclipse integrated development environment, and can be operated seamlessly with existing plugins on Eclipse.  Overview and System Construction Flow  Installation and Startup  Views (Overview)  Views (Name Service View)  Views (Repository View)  Views (Configuration View)  Views (Manager Control View)  Views (Execution Context View)  Views (Composite Component View)  Views (Log View)  Views (Property View)  System Editor (Basic Operations)  System Editor (Composite Components)  System Editor (Save)  System Editor (RTC Display / Drawing Editing)  System Editor (Connecting Ports)  Offline System Editor  Settings Screen  Other
