title: Compilation Method (Windows, Using CMake, C++)
content: This section explains how to build on Windows.#contentsPreparing the EnvironmentEnvironment      Visual C++ (version 2005 or later)    VC++ development environment        CMake (version 2.8.5 or later)    A tool for generating build files suitable for the development environment        Doxygen    Documentation generator        Graphviz    A tool for outputting graph structures written in the dot language as images        Wix Windows Installer XML toolset (version 3.5 or later)    A toolset for creating Windows Installer (MSI) packages  If the directories where Wix and Graphviz are installed (C:\Program Files (x86)\WiX Toolset v3.11\bin, C:\Program Files (x86)\Graphviz2.44.1\bin) are not set in the PATH environment variable, set them.After installing Graphviz, check the plugin registration status with the dot -v command. For the procedure, see this page.Build ProcedureThe build procedure is shown below.The figures use VC++ 2017 and CMake 3.14.1.CMake SettingsStart the GUI version of CMake and specify the directories.      Where is the source code    Specify the folder containing the code generated by RTCBuilder.        Where to build the binaries    Specify the folder where files such as the solution, project, and workspace files will be output.  Specifying the DirectoriesRunning ConfigureClick the [Configure] button to run it. Then select the platform to use.In this example, “Visual Studio 15 2017” is selected.Selecting the PlatformEnabling BUILD_DOCUMENTATIONEnable the BUILD_DOCUMENTATION option to generate documentation.Enabling BUILD_DOCUMENTATIONRunning GenerateAfter Configure completes successfully, click the [Generate] button.Running GenerateRunning VC++Press the [Open Project] button to open the solution file (*.sln).Running the BuildRun [Build] > [Build Solution] to build the solution.Running the BuildDocumentation Generation ProcedureRunning doxygenIn Solution Explorer, select “doc” and right-click it.Then select “Build” and run it.Running doxygenDocumentationThe documentation is generated in doc/html/doxygen/html under the folder specified in “Where to build the binaries”.Documentation ExamplePackage Generation ProcedurePackage generation uses cpack, which is included with CMake, and Wix.Running the PACKAGE BuildIn Solution Explorer, select “PACKAGE” and right-click it.Then select “Build” and run it.Running the PACKAGE BuildPackageAn msi-format installation package is generated under the folder specified in “Where to build the binaries”._rtm120_win64.msiWhen this installation package is executed, it is installed in the following location.`C:\Program Files\OpenRTM-aist\1.2.0\Components\\\`

title: Screen Layout and Functions (RT Profile Editor)
content: #contentsThis section explains the RT Profile Editor.RT Profile Editor　The RT Profile Editor consists of the following pages.RT Profile Editor Configuration      No.    Screen Component Name    Description        1    Basic Profile Input Page    Enter basic component information, such as profile information for the RT component.        2    Activity Profile    Specify information such as the activities supported by the RT component.        3    Data Port Profile    Enter profiles for the data ports attached to the RT component.        4    Service Port Profile    Enter profiles for the service ports attached to the RT component and the service interfaces attached to the service ports.        5    Configuration    Enter user-defined configuration parameter information and system configuration information to be set for the RT component.        6    Documentation Generation    Enter various documentation information to be added to the RT component to be generated.        7    Language/Environment    Enter information about the code selection to be generated and the execution environment, such as the OS.        8    RTC.xml    Displays and edits the RtcProfile generated based on the configured information in XML format.  You can switch between pages by selecting the tabs at the bottom of the editor screen.Basic Profile Input PageThis page is used to enter basic component information, such as profile information for the RT component.Basic Profile Input PageEach input item is described below.Basic Profile Input Page Item Descriptions      Item    Description    Required        RT-Component Basic Profile        Module Name    This is the name that identifies the RT component. This is a required input item. This name is used as the component name in the generated source code. Only alphanumeric characters can be entered.    ○        Module Description    A brief overview of the RT component.    -        Version    The version of the RT component. In principle, enter the version number in a format such as x.y.z.    -        Vendor Name    The name of the vendor that developed the RT component.    ○        Module Category    The category of the RT component.    ○        Component Type    The type of the RT component. It can be specified from the following options.・STATIC: A type of RTC that exists statically. Dynamic creation and deletion are not performed.・UNIQUE: A type of RTC that can be dynamically created and deleted, but each component has an internal unique state and is not necessarily interchangeable.・COMMUTATIVE: A type of RTC that can be dynamically created and deleted, and because it has no internal state, generated components are interchangeable.    ○        Activity Type    The activity type of the RT component. It can be specified from the following options.・PERIODIC: An activity type that executes RTC actions at regular intervals・SPORADIC: An activity type that executes RTC actions irregularly・EVENT_DRIVEN: An activity type in which RTC actions are event-driven    ○        Component Kind    The type of execution form of the RT component. It can be selected from the following options. (Multiple options can be combined)・DataFlow: An execution form that executes actions periodically・FSM: An execution form that executes actions according to external events・MultiMode: An execution form that has multiple operation modes    ○        Maximum Number of Instances    The maximum number of RT component instances. Enter a natural number.    -        Execution Type    The type of ExecutionContext. It can be selected from the following.・PeriodicExecutionContext: ExecutionContext that performs periodic execution・ExtTrigExecutionContext: ExecutionContext that performs execution by an external trigger    ○        Execution Rate    The execution rate of the ExecutionContext. A positive double value can be entered (unit: Hz).    -        Description    A description of the RT component.    －        RTC Type    Specify this when it is necessary to distinguish RT components that implement specific functions.    －  Activity Profile Input PageThis page is used to enter information about the activities supported by the RT component to be generated.Activity Profile Input PageThe contents of the Documentation section are set for each activity. The Documentation section displays the content corresponding to the currently selected activity.Each input item is described below.Activity Profile Input Page Item Descriptions      Item    Description    Required        Activity Profile        onInitialize    Initialization processing. It is called only once at the start of the component lifecycle.    -        onFinalize    Finalization processing. It is called only once at the end of the component lifecycle.    －        onStartup    Called only once when the ExecutionContext starts execution.    －        onShutdown    Called only once when the ExecutionContext stops execution.    －        onActivated    Called only once when transitioning from the inactive state to the active state.    －        onDeactivated    Called only once when transitioning from the active state to the inactive state.    －        onAborting    Called only once before entering the ERROR state.    －        onError    Called while in the ERROR state.    －        onReset    Called only once when resetting from the ERROR state and transitioning to the inactive state.    －        onExecute    Called periodically while in the active state.    －        onStateUpdate    Called every time after on_execute.    －        onRateChanged    Called when the rate of the ExecutionContext is changed.    －        onAction    Called to execute an operation according to the corresponding state.    －        onModeChanged    Called when the mode is changed.    －        Documentation        Activity Name    Displays the name of the currently selected activity.    －        Operation Overview    Describe an overview of the operation executed by the target activity.    －        Preconditions    Describe the preconditions that must be satisfied before executing the target activity.    －        Postconditions    Describe the postconditions that are satisfied after executing the target activity. However, if the target activity is executed when the preconditions are not satisfied, satisfaction of the postconditions is not guaranteed.    －  Data Port Profile Input PageThis page is used to enter information about the data ports attached to the RT component.Data Port Profile Input PageTo add a new port (InPort/OutPort), click the [Add] button in each section.You can also delete the selected port by clicking the [Delete] button in each section.The contents of the documentation section can be set for each port. The documentation section displays the content corresponding to the selected port.Each input item is described below.Data Port Profile Input Page Item Descriptions      Item    Description    Required        DataPort Profile        Port Name    The name of the DataPort. Only half-width alphanumeric characters can be entered.Port names cannot overlap with Data OutPort or Service Port names.    ○        Detail        Port Name    Displays the currently selected Data Port in the format "port name (InPort/OutPort)".    －        Data Type    The data type handled by the DataPort.Data types defined in the IDL specified on the settings screen can be used.    ○        Variable Name    The variable name corresponding to the DataPort.    －        Display Position    The display position of the Data InPort in the Build View.    ○        Overview Description    Describe an overview of the data port.    －        Data Type    Describe the type handled by the data port.    －        Number of Data    Describe the number of data items, such as when the data is an array.    －        Meaning    Describe the meaning of the data.    －        Unit    Describe the unit of the data.    －        Occurrence Frequency/Cycle    Describe the occurrence frequency and cycle of the data.    －        Processing Speed/Cycle    Describe the processing speed and processing cycle of the data.    －  Service Port Profile Input PageThis page is used to enter information about the service ports attached to the RT component.Service Port Profile Input Page (Service Port Information Input)Service Port Profile Input Page (Service Interface Information Input)A new service port can be added by selecting “Add Port” in the “RT-Component Service Ports” field on the left side of the screen.With a service port selected in “RT-Component Service Ports” on the left side of the screen, you can add a new service interface by selecting “Add Interface”.With a service port or service interface selected in “RT-Component Service Ports” on the left side of the screen, you can delete the selected port/interface by selecting [Delete].Each input item is described below.Service Port Profile Input Page Item Descriptions (Service Port)      Item    Description    Required        RT-Component Service Port Profile        Port Name    The name of the service port. Only half-width alphanumeric characters can be entered.Data InPort, Data OutPort, and Service Port names cannot overlap.    ○        Display Position    The display position of the service port in the Build View.    ○        Documentation        Overview Description    Describe an overview of the service port.    －        I/F Overview Description    Describe an overview of the service interfaces attached to the service port.    －  Service Port Profile Input Page Item Descriptions (Service Port)      Item    Description    Required        RT-Component Service Port Interface Profile        Interface Name    The name of the service interface. Only half-width alphanumeric characters can be entered.Service interface names cannot overlap.    ○        Direction    The type of service interface. It can be selected from the following options.・Provided: Provided interface (for Service Provider)・Required: Required interface (for Service Consumer)    ○        Instance Name    The instance name of the service interface. Only half-width alphanumeric characters can be entered.    ○        Variable Name    The variable name of the service interface. If omitted, the instance name is used.    －        IDL File    Specifies the IDL file name used for the service interface. Clicking the [Browse...] button displays a file selection dialog.    ○        Interface Type    The service type used for the service interface. When an IDL file is specified, type information defined in the IDL is displayed. Only half-width alphanumeric characters can be entered.    ○        IDL Path    The IDL search path. Clicking the [Browse...] button displays a directory selection dialog.    －        Documentation        Overview Description    Describe an overview of the service interface.    －        Arguments    Describe the arguments of the service interface.    －        Return Value    Describe the return value of the service interface.    －        Exceptions    Describe the exceptions of the service interface.    －        Preconditions    Describe the preconditions that must be satisfied before executing the operation of the service interface.    －        Postconditions    Describe the postconditions that are satisfied after executing the operation of the service interface.    －  Configuration Profile Input PageThis page is used to enter user-defined configuration parameter information and other system configuration information to be set for the RT component.Configuration Profile Input PageTo add new user-defined configuration parameter information and system configuration information, click the [Add] button in each section.You can also delete the selected configuration information by clicking the [Delete] button in each section.The contents of the Detail section and Documentation section can be set for each user-defined configuration parameter.Each section displays the content configured for the selected user-defined configuration parameter.Each input item is described below.Configuration Profile Input Page Item Descriptions      Item    Description    Required        RT-Component Configuration Parameter Definitions        Name    The name of the user-defined configuration parameter. Only half-width alphanumeric characters can be entered.User-defined configuration parameter names cannot overlap.    ○        Detail        Parameter Name    Displays the currently selected user-defined configuration parameter.    －        Data Type    The data type of the user-defined configuration parameter.Data types defined in the IDL specified on the settings screen can be used.    ○        Default Value    The default value of the user-defined configuration parameter. Any value, including two-byte characters, can be set.    ○        Variable Name    The variable name of the user-defined configuration parameter. Only half-width alphanumeric characters can be entered.    －        Unit    The unit of the user-defined configuration parameter.    －        Constraint    Describe the constraint conditions for the user-defined configuration parameter. For how to describe constraint conditions, see [[Constraint Information Description Format>#seiyaku]].    －        Widget    Specifies the control used when setting configuration parameters in the ConfigurationView of RTSystemEditor. It can be selected from the following values.・text: Text box (default setting)・slider: Slider・spin: Spin button・radio: Radio button・check: Checkbox・ordered_list: Ordered list    ○        Step    When "slider" is selected as the input control, specifies the step width of the slider.    －        Parameter Name    Displays the currently selected user-defined configuration parameter.    －        Data Name    Describe the name of the user-defined configuration parameter.    －        Default Value    Describe the default value of the user-defined configuration parameter.    －        Overview Description    Describe an overview of the user-defined configuration parameter.    －        Unit    Describe the unit of the user-defined configuration parameter.    －        Data Range    Describe the data range of the user-defined configuration parameter.    －        Constraint    Describe the constraint conditions of the user-defined configuration parameter.    －        RT-Component Configuration Parameter        Configuration    The configuration name to be set. Select it from the list.    ○        Default Value    The default value of the configuration to be set. For items that already have default values set, the default value is set when the name is selected.    －  Documentation Information Settings PageEnter various documentation information related to the RT component to be generated.Documentation Information Input PageThe information entered on this page is embedded in the generated code in doxygen format.Each input item is described below.Documentation Information Settings Page Item Descriptions      Item    Description    Required        Component Overview        Overview Description    Describe an overview of the RT component to be generated.    －        Input/Output    Describe an overview of the input/output of the RT component.    －        Algorithms, etc.    Describe the algorithms and other items used by the RT component.    －        Other        Author/Contact    Describe information about the author and contact of the RT component.    －        License/Terms of Use    Describe information about the license and terms of use of the RT component.    －        References    Describe reference information.    －        Version Upgrade Log        VersionUp Log    Describe log information related to the changes made this time.    －        License/Terms of Use    Displays log information from past version upgrades.    －  Language/Environment Information Input PageThis page is used to enter the language selection for the template source code generated based on the entered RT component specifications, the execution environment such as OS, dependent libraries, and so on.Language/Environment Information Input PageSections are divided by the language to be generated. Select the section for the language you want to generate, and enter the setting information specific to each language.When one section is selected, all other sections are closed.When code generation is executed (when the [Generate Code] button on the Basic Profile input page is clicked), template code for the language of the selected section is generated.Each input item is described below.Language/Environment Information Input Page Item Descriptions      Item    Description    Required        Language    Specifies the language to be generated.    ○        Use old build environment.    When this checkbox is turned ON, code similar to the old version (a format that does not use Cmake) is generated.    －        Environment        Version    Sets the version information of the language in which the RTC to be generated is implemented.    －        OS    Sets OS information on which the RTC to be generated runs.    －        OS Version    Sets version information for the OS on which the RTC to be generated runs.    －        CPU    Sets CPU architecture information on which the RTC to be generated runs.    －        Other OS Information    Sets supplementary information other than version information for the OS on which the RTC to be generated runs.    －        Other CPU Information    Sets supplementary information other than architecture information for the CPU on which the RTC to be generated runs.    －        Library Information        Name    Specifies the name of the external library used by the RTC to be generated.    ○        Version    Specifies version information for the external library used by the RTC to be generated.    －        Info.    Specifies supplementary information for the external library used by the RTC to be generated.    －  When you click the [Add] button, an item row is added to the list. Then, when you click the added row, a file selection dialog is displayed, so select the target file.RTC Profile XML Editing PageThis page is used to check and edit the contents of the XML file (RTC.xml) that describes the entered RT component specifications.It is used to check the settings configured on other pages and to directly edit items that cannot be entered from the GUI screen.Language/Environment Information Input PageThe content of the displayed RT component specifications is created based on the content configured on other pages when switching to this page.Clicking the [Update] button at the upper right of the screen reflects the content set or changed on this page in the other pages (it only reflects the content in the other pages and does not write to the file).A screen like the following is also displayed, allowing you to check the changes. To reflect the changes in the other pages, click [OK].XML Edit Content Comparison ScreenThe content entered directly on this page is saved only when it is saved while this page is displayed.If you edit the content on this page and then save while another page is open, the items entered on the other page take precedence.When saving the content of this page, validation is performed according to the schema definition of RTC.xml.If an error is found during validation, an error message like the following is displayed, so correct the relevant location by referring to the displayed content.Example of an XML Validation Error&aname(seiyaku);Constraint Information Description FormatConstraint conditions for data ports and user-defined configuration parameters are set in the following format.Constraint Condition Description Format      Setting Content    Setting Format        None    Blank        100 (literal value)    100        100 or more    x >= 100        100 or less    x<=100        Greater than 100    x>100        Less than 100    x<100        100 or more and 200 or less    100<=x<=200        Greater than 100 and less than 200    100<x<200        Enumeration Type    (9600,19200,115200)        Array Type    x>100, x>200, x>300        Hash Type    {key0: 100<x<200, key1: x>=100}

title: Creating an msi with CPack (Windows)
content: #contents(4)IntroductionThe msi installer is created by building with Visual Studio.Creation Procedure When Not Including doxygen Documentation  By default, the documentation build is OFF, so it is not generated.From Solution Explorer in Visual Studio, right-click “PACKAGE”, select “Build”, and execute it.Creation Procedure When Including doxygen DocumentationChange the following line in CMakeLists.txt directly under the project folder from OFF to ON.For a C++ RTC, this is around line 86, and for a Python RTC, around line 77. option(BUILD_DOCUMENTATION "Build the documentation" ON) ※この行の OFF を ON に書き換えます。(デフォルトは OFF)  From Solution Explorer in Visual Studio, right-click “doc”, select “Build”, and execute it.  After the build of “doc” is complete, right-click “PACKAGE” and select “Build”.[Notes]  Confirm that “BUILD_DOCUMENTATION” is checked in CMake configure.  Build “doc” first, and then build “PACKAGE”. If you build “PACKAGE” without building “doc”, an error will occur.msi Installer Storage Location and File NameIf it is created successfully, it will be saved in [build] under the project directory.The file name will be “RTC project name + RTC version number_OpenRTM-aist version number_architecture”.(Example) Flip100_rtm120_win64.msi  The architecture will be [win32] or [win64].　The version number is in a format with dots removed; [1.0.0] becomes [100].Installing and Uninstalling an msiInstallation  Double-click the created msi installer.  Click [Next].  Check [I accept the license agreement] and click [Next].  Click [Next].The default installation path is as follows.(Example) C:\Program Files\OpenRTM-aist\1.2.0\Components\c++\ImageProcessing<br>          ImageProcessing is the name specified in “Module Category” in RTCBuilder.        Click [Install] to start the installation.  Click [Finish] to exit the installer. After installation, it will be registered in the Start menu.GUID Settings for UpgradesWhen upgrading, it is necessary to set a GUID in order to check the version that is already installed.Because the GUID is not set by default, a new GUID is assigned every time PACKAGE is built in Visual Studio.By setting the GUID in advance, it is possible to determine whether it is an upgrade or a new installation.The procedure for setting the GUID is shown below.  From Solution Explorer in Visual Studio, right-click “PACKAGE”, select “Build”, and execute it.  When the build is complete, the GUID will be displayed in the output screen below. Select it and copy it.  From Solution Explorer, expand “ALL_BILD” and click CMakeLists.txt.  Paste the GUID copied in step 2 as shown in the following screen, and overwrite-save CMakeLists.txt.  Again, from Solution Explorer, right-click “PACKAGE”, select “Build”, and execute it.[Supplement]In addition to the above, there is also a method of creating a new GUID.From the Visual Studio menu, select [Tools] > [Create GUID] to display the “Create GUID” dialog.  In [GUID format], select [4. Registry Format…].  Click the [New GUID] button.  Click the [Copy] button.  Click the [Exit] button to close the dialog.  Paste it into CMakeLists.txt as shown in the following screen and overwrite-save it. * Paste only the numbers.UninstallationThe uninstallation procedure is as follows.How to Remove from Control Panel  Open [Control Panel] and click [Uninstall a program].  Select the installed package name and click [Uninstall].  If the display has disappeared from the list in Control Panel, uninstallation is complete.    How to Remove from the Installer    Double-click the created msi installer.  Click [Remove].  Click [Remove].  Click [Finish] to exit the installer.IDL Compilation Processing for Python RTCs with Service PortsPython RTCs with service ports execute IDL compilation when the package is installed.This behavior is implemented by idlcompile.bat and delete.bat in the project folder during IDL compilation execution, so be careful not to delete these files, as the function will stop working.By uninstalling from Control Panel, files generated after IDL compilation execution will also be deleted.The following is a list of files installed by the msi installer. Files marked with ★ are generated by IDL compilation. tree /f インストールディレクトリー\OpenRTM-aist\1.2.0\Components\Python\Category\FlipGUI C:\インストールディレクトリー\OpenRTM-aist\1.2.0\Components\Python\Category\FlipGUI │  BasicDataType_idl.py ★ │  CalibrationService_idl.py ★ │  delete.bat │  ExtendedDataTypes_idl.py ★ │  idlcompile.bat │  InterfaceDataTypes_idl.py ★ │  RTC.xml │  rtutil.py │  setup.py │  flipgui.py │  FlipGUIComp.py │ ├─idl │   BasicDataType.idl │   CalibrationService.idl │   CMakeLists.txt │   ExtendedDataTypes.idl │   InterfaceDataTypes.idl │ ├─ImageCalibService ★ │   __init__.py ★ │ ├─ImageCalibService__POA ★ │   __init__.py ★ │ ├─RTC ★ │   __init__.py ★ │ └─RTC__POA ★       __init__.py ★

title: Code Generation, Save, and Load
content: #contentsCode GenerationAfter setting various profile information for the RT component to be generated, generate the template code.When you click the [Generate Code] button on the Basic Profile input page, template code corresponding to the entered profile information is generated.Generating Template CodeThe template files generated when code generation is executed after selecting each language are as follows.List of Generated Files  C++ (when the “Use old build environment.” checkbox is not selected)      File Name    Description        <RTC name> Comp.cpp    Code for starting the RT component.        <RTC name>.h    Header of the RT component body.        <RTC name>.cpp    Code of the RT component body.        <service type name>SVC_impl.h    Header of the service provider. (*)Only the Type specified in ServiceProvider is output.        <service type name>SVC_impl. cpp    Implementation code of the service provider. (*)Only the Type specified in ServiceProvider is output.        CMakeLists.txt    Configuration file for CMake.        doc/        doxyfile.in    Configuration file for Doxygen.        cmake/        uninstall_target.cmake.in    Template file for adding an uninstall target (for CMake)        cpack_options.cmake    Module for creating WiX packages (for CMake/WiX)        License.rtf    License display included in package information (for CMake/WiX)        wix.xsl.in    Template for specifying files to include in the WiX package (for CMake/WiX)        cmake/Modules/        FindOpenRTM.cmake    Module for obtaining OpenRTM-aist environment settings (for CMake)    C++ (when the [Use old build environment.] checkbox is selected)      File Name    Description        <RTC name> Comp.cpp    Code for starting the RT component.        <RTC name>.h    Header of the RT component body.        <RTC name>.cpp    Code of the RT component body.        <service type name>SVC_impl.h    Header of the service provider. (*)Only the Type specified in ServiceProvider is output.        <service type name>SVC_impl. cpp    Implementation code of the service provider. (*)Only the Type specified in ServiceProvider is output.        Makefile.<RTC name>    Makefile for compiling.        <RTC name> _vc8.sln     Solution file for Visual Studio 2005.        <RTC name>_vc8.vcproj    RT component project file for Visual Studio 2005.        <RTC name>Comp_vc8.vcproj    Project file for startup code for Visual Studio 2005.        <RTC name>_vc9.sln    Solution file for Visual Studio 2008.        <RTC name>_vc9.vcproj    RT component project file for Visual Studio 2008.        <RTC name>Comp_vc9.vcproj    Project file for startup code for Visual Studio 2008.        Copyprops.bat    Batch file for copying property files.        User_config.vsprops    User-defined property file.        OpenRTM-aist.vsprops    Property file for OpenRTM-aist.    Java      File Name    Description        <RTC name>Comp.java    Class for starting the RT component.        <RTC name>.java    Class that defines the RT component's Component Profile, initialization processing, and so on.        <RTC name>Impl.java    Main body of the RT component.        build_<RTC name>.xml    Build file for the RT component.        <service type name> SVC_impl.java    Implementation class of the service provider. (*)        CMakeLists.txt    Configuration file for CMake.        doc/        doxyfile.in    Configuration file for Doxygen.        cmake_modules/        cmake_javacompile.cmake.in    Template file for adding a Java compile target (for CMake)        FindOpenRTMJava.cmake    Module for obtaining OpenRTM-aist-Java environment settings (for CMake)        cmake/        uninstall_target.cmake.in    Template file for adding an uninstall target (for CMake)        cpack_options.cmake    Module for creating WiX packages (for CMake/WiX)        License.rtf    License display included in package information (for CMake/WiX)        cpack_resources/        wix.xsl.in    Template for specifying files to include in the WiX package (for CMake/WiX)    Python      File Name    Description        <RTC name>.py    Code of the RT component.        <service type name>_idl.py        <service type name>_idl_example.py    Implementation file of the service provider. (*)        CMakeLists.txt    Configuration file for CMake.        doc/        doxyfile.in    Configuration file for Doxygen.        cmake_modules/        FindOpenRTMPython.cmake    Module for obtaining OpenRTM-aist-Python environment settings (for CMake)        cmake/        uninstall_target.cmake.in    Template file for adding an uninstall target (for CMake)        cpack_options.cmake    Module for creating WiX packages (for CMake/WiX)        License.rtf    License display included in package information (for CMake/WiX)        cpack_resources/        Description.txt    Description included in package information (for CMake)        License.txt    License display included in package information (for CMake/Linux)        wix.xsl.in    Template for specifying files to include in the WiX package (for CMake/WiX)    When outputting the service provider implementation file, RtcBuilder parses the IDL in order to generate operation templates. However, this parsing function has the following limitations.  In the preprocessor, only the #include directive can be used. (#ifdef and similar directives are simply ignored.)  The generated operations are only the operations of the directly specified interface, and do not include operations inherited from parent interfaces.Output SelectionIf a file with the same name as a generated file already exists in the output destination, and there is a difference in output content between the existing file and the generated file, RtcBuilder displays a confirmation screen for selecting which output to use.Output Selection ScreenIn output selection, select from the following three output candidates.  Original: Leave the existing file as-is  Merge: Perform merging using merge blocks (Note 1)  Generate: Overwrite with the newly generated contentNote 1 In Merge, only the range enclosed by the <rtc-template block=”block”> tag is overwritten with the latest generated content. In the generated template, the range that users should not modify is enclosed with this tag in advance.Anything inside this tag will disappear after modification when merged, so do not modify it.Perspective SwitchingIf a development environment plugin for the target generation language is installed, a confirmation message for switching perspectives is displayed after code generation is executed.If the target plugin is installed, a message like the following is displayed, so select whether or not to switch perspectives.Perspective Switching Confirmation MessageThe relationship between the generation language and the development environment plugin is as follows.  Java: JDT (Java Development Tools) → A development environment included in Eclipse in advance.  C++: CDT (C/C++ Development Tooling)  Python: PyDevNote: If a development environment plugin for each language is installed and the output target project is a newly created project, the attributes of the target language are set in the properties of each project.Packaging Function for Generated FilesThis function archives generated template files, executable binary files of RT components created based on template files, and other artifacts in various formats.When you click the [Package] button on the Basic Profile input page, the “RT Component Packaging” screen for setting packaging details is displayed.Packaging Function for Various ArtifactsRT Component Packaging ScreenEach item is explained below.RT Component Packaging Screen Item Descriptions      Item    Description        Target Project    Select the project to be packaged.        Destination Directory    Enter the directory to output the packaged artifacts. By using the "Browse" button, a directory selection dialog is displayed.        Archive Method    Select the format of the archive to be created.        Options    Overview description of the behavior within each action. This item can be omitted.        Archive Format    It is possible to create archives using the ZIP format and archives using the tar format. Select the format to use.        Compress Archive Contents    If you want to compress the archive contents, turn on the checkbox.        Directory Structure    Select whether to archive while preserving the directory structure of the target project as-is, or to archive with everything placed in the root directory.  Note: For each archive method (“source”, “binary”, “source + binary”), which file types are included in the archive can be configured on the “Settings Screen” described later.Saving and Loading SettingsRTCBuilder can save the content entered in the RTC Profile Editor to an RTC profile XML (RTC.xml), and can load the saved content again.SaveThe content entered in the RTC Profile Editor can be saved to an RTC profile XML (RTC.xml). The entered content can be saved by the following operations.  Right-click the editor and select [Save] or [Save As…] from the displayed context menu  Select [File] > [Save…] or [File] > [Save As…] from the menu barNote: If [Save As…] is selected, it can be saved in any project.                  Save  LoadThe RTC profile XML (RTC.xml) that stores the content of the RTC Profile Editor can be loaded by the following operations.  Right-click the editor and select [Open] from the context menu  Select [File] > [Open File…] from the menu bar                  Load

title: Screen Layout and Functions (Overview)
content: RTCBuilder has the following screen layout.#clearRTC Builder Screen ComponentsList of Screen Components      No.    Screen Component Name    Description        1    RTC Profile Editor    Edits profiles, data port definitions, service port definitions, configuration definitions, and other extended profiles that constitute the specifications of an RT component.        2    Build View    Graphically displays the RT component being edited, as well as data ports, service ports, and service interfaces, using icons.        3    Repository View    Displays information about the selected RT repository.

title: Various Settings
content: #contentsThis section explains the various settings of RTCBuilder.The RTCBuilder settings screen is displayed by selecting “RTCBuilder” from the “Preferences” screen, which is displayed by selecting [Window] > [Preferences…] from the menu at the top of the screen.Data TypeYou can set the location of the IDL files that define the data types configured for Data Port and Configuration parameters.To add a new IDL storage directory, click the [New] button. You can also delete the selected IDL storage directory by clicking the [Remove] button.Select the actual location of the IDL storage directory in the directory selection screen that appears when you click inside the “IDL File Directories” field.RTCBuilder Settings ScreenCode GenerationYou can set the default contents that are configured when a new editor is displayed or a new item is added on the Basic Profile input page and Configuration Profile input page of the RTC Profile Editor.Code Generation Settings ScreenThe default settings on this settings screen (the contents set when the [Restore Defaults] button is clicked) are as follows.Code Generation Settings Screen Default Values      Item    Default Value        >    Basic        Component name    ModuleName        Description    ModuleDescription        Version    1.0.0        Vendor    VendorName        Category    Category        Component Type    STATIC        Component’s activity type    PERIODIC        Max. Instances    1        Component kind    DataFlowComponent        Execution type    PeriodicExecutionContext        Execution rate    1.0        >    Configuration        Name    conf_name        Type    conf_type        Variable Name    conf_varname        Default Value    conf_default        Constraint    conf_constraint        Unit  PortYou can set the default contents that are configured when a new item is added on the Data Port Profile input page and Service Port Profile input page of the RTC Profile Editor.Port Settings ScreenThe default settings on this settings screen (the contents set when the [Restore Defaults] button is clicked) are as follows.Port Settings Screen Default Values      Item    Default Value        Data Port        DataPort Name    dp_name        DataPort Type    dp_type        DataPort Variable Name    dp_vname        DataPort Constraint    dp_constraint        DataPort Unit            Service Port        ServicePort Name    sv_name        Service Interface        Interface Name    if_name        Instance Name    if_instance        Variable Name    if_varname  ConfigurationYou can set the items displayed in the system configuration information on the Configuration Profile input page of the RTC Profile Editor.Configuration Settings ScreenThe default settings on this settings screen (the contents set when the [Restore Defaults] button is clicked) are as follows.Configuration Settings Screen Default Values      Item    Default Value        exec_cxt.periodic.type    PeriodicExecutionContext        exec_cxt.periodic.rate    1000        exec_cxt.evdriven.type    EventDrivenExecutionContext  ExportYou can set the files to be included in each archive format of the RT component packaging function.Export Settings ScreenThe settings screen is divided into sections for each archive format (Source Export, Binary Export, Source+Binary Export). Each section consists of an extension specification area and a file name specification area.Export Settings Screen (Section)In the extension specification area, you can set the extensions of files to be included in each archive format. When you click the [Select Types] button, a type selection screen like the following is displayed. Select the file types you want to include in the archive.              * Only registered extensions are displayed in the file extension list. If you want to select files that do not exist in the list, enter the corresponding extensions in the "Other extensions" field at the bottom of the screen, separated by ",".  Extension Selection ScreenIn the file setting area, you can set the file names to be included in the archive. When you click the [Add] button at the bottom of the “File name” list, a new row is added, so directly enter the file name you want to include in the archive. You can also delete the selected row by clicking the [Delete] button.In the example shown in Export Settings Screen (Section) above, when “Source+Binary” is selected as the archive method, files with the extensions “cpp” and “h” and files with the names “Makefile” and “README” are included in the archive.The default settings on this settings screen (the contents set when the [Restore Defaults] button is clicked) are as follows.Export Settings Screen Default Values      Item    Default Value        Source Export        Extension    conf, cpp, h, vcproj, java, xml, py        File Name    Makefile, README        Binary Export        Extension    conf, exe, class, py        File Name    README        Source+Binary Export        Extension    conf, cpp, h, vcproj, java, xml, py, exe, class        File Name    Makefile, README  Build ViewYou can set the color information of the icons displayed in the Build View.Build View Settings ScreenEach color setting button allows you to change the color settings for the component body, DataInPort, DataOutPort, ServicePort, and ServiceInterface.DocumentYou can set the enabled/disabled attributes (ON/OFF) for each activity.Document Settings Screen

title: Creating a deb with CPack (Linux)
content: #contentsIntroductionThe procedure for creating a deb package is shown below.Creation Procedure When Not Including doxygen Documentation      By default, the documentation build is OFF, so it is not generated.        For a C++ RTC   $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー $ mkdir build $ cd build $ cmake .. $ make $ cpack  For a Pyrhon RTC $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー $ mkdir build $ cd build $ cmake .. $ cpackCreation Procedure When Including doxygen DocumentationChange the following line in CMakeLists.txt directly under the project directory from OFF to ON.For a C++ RTC, this is around line 86, and for a Python RTC, around line 77. option(BUILD_DOCUMENTATION "Build the documentation" ON) ※この行の OFF を ON に書き換えます。(デフォルトは OFF)  For a C++ RTC $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー $ mkdir build $ cd build $ cmake .. $ make $ make doc $ cpack  For a Pyrhon RTC $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー $ mkdir build $ cd build $ cmake .. $ make doc $ cpack[Notes]If you turn ON the documentation build and run “cpack” without running “make doc”, the following error will occur. CMake Error at /home/プロジェクトディレクトリー/build/doc/cmake_install.cmake:36 (file): file INSTALL cannot find "/home/プロジェクトディレクトリー/build/doc/html/doxygen/html".deb Package Storage Location and File NameIf it is created successfully, it will be saved in [build] under the project directory.The file name will be “RTC project name_RTC version number_architecture”.(Example) Flip_1.2.0_amd64.deb  The architecture will be [i386] or [amd64].How to Check a deb Package  When checking a deb package with the less command $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー/build  $ less Flip_1.2.0_amd64.deb Flip_1.2.0_amd64.deb 新形式 debian パッケージ、バージョン 2.0。 サイズ 258304 バイト: コントロールアーカイブ = 2797 バイト。     162 バイト、    9 行      control                 10062 バイト、   92 行      md5sums               Package: affine Version: 1.2.0 Section: devel Priority: optional Architecture: amd64 Installed-Size: 884 Maintainer: unknown　※パッケージメンテナー情報を定義していないと「unknown」になります Description: Flip image componentPress “q” to exit less.  When extracting and checking the contents of a deb packageIf the tree command is not installed, install it. $ sudo apt-get install tree $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー/build  $ dpkg -x Flip_1.2.0_amd64.deb . $ tree usr usr └─ share    　└─ openrtm-1.2        　　└─ components            　　　└─ python               　　　 　└─ Category　※指定したインストール先ディレクトリー                    　　　　　└─ FlipGUI                        　　　　　　├─ RTC.xml                        　　　　　　├─ FlipGUIComp.py                        　　　　　　├─ idl                        　　　　　　│    ├─ BasicDataType.idl                        　　　　　　│    ├─ CMakeLists.txt                     　　　　　　   │    ├─ CalibrationService.idl                  　　　　　　      │    ├─ ExtendedDataTypes.idl                        　　　　　　│    └─ InterfaceDataTypes.idl                        　　　　　　├─ idlcompile.sh                      　　　　　　  ├─ rtutil.py                        　　　　　　├─ setup.py                        　　　　　　└─ flipgui.pyInstalling and Uninstalling a deb PackageInstallationRun the following command to install. $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー/build  $ sudo dpkg -i Flip_1.2.0_amd64.deb UninstallationRun the following command to uninstall. $ sudo dpkg -ｒ FlipIDL Compilation Processing for Python RTCs with Service PortsPython RTCs with service ports execute IDL compilation when the package is installed.This behavior is implemented by postinst.in and prerm.in in the project directory during IDL compilation execution, so be careful not to delete these files, as the function will stop working.The following is a list of files installed from the deb package. Files marked with ★ are generated by IDL compilation. $ tree /usr/share/openrtm-1.2/components/python/Category/FlipGUI/ /usr/share/openrtm-1.2/components/python/Category/FlipGUI/   ├─ BasicDataType_idl.py  ★   ├─ CalibrationService_idl.py  ★   ├─ ExtendedDataTypes_idl.py  ★   ├─ ImageCalibService  ★   │   └─ __init__.py  ★   ├─ ImageCalibService__POA  ★   │   └─ __init__.py  ★   ├─ InterfaceDataTypes_idl.py  ★   ├─ RTC  ★   │   └─ __init__.py  ★   ├─ RTC.xml   ├─ RTC__POA  ★   │   └─ __init__.py  ★   ├─ FlipGUIComp.py   ├─ idl   │   ├─ BasicDataType.idl   │   ├─ CMakeLists.txt   │   ├─ CalibrationService.idl   │   ├─ ExtendedDataTypes.idl   │   └─ InterfaceDataTypes.idl   ├─ idlcompile.sh   ├─ rtutil.py   ├─ setup.py   └─ flipgui.py

title: Package Creation Using CPack (Common Settings for Windows/Linux)
content: #contents(4)IntroductionCMake has a function for creating installer packages with CPack.RT components generated using OpenRTP 1.2.0 or later can be made into installer packages without changing the CMake settings generated by RTCBuilder.In a Windows environment, you can create an msi-format installer; in a Linux Ubuntu or Debian environment, you can create a deb package; and in a Fedora environment, you can create an rpm package.(Note) However, with OpenRTP 1.2.0, packages can be created only for C++ or Python RTCs, and Java RTCs are not supported.Installation of OpenRTP 1.2.0 is introduced on the download page for OpenRTM-aist 1.2.0.PreparationInstall the software required for creating installers and packages.Windows EnvironmentIn addition to the software shown when installing OpenRTM-aist, the following software must be installed.      WiX Toolset    Required to create msi installers.        Graphviz    Allows flowcharts, system diagrams, and similar diagrams to be included in documentation.  Installing WiX Toolset  Start the installer and click the [install] button to begin installation.#ref(WiX Toolset 1-1.png,70%,center)  When “Complete” is displayed on the [install] button, installation is complete. Click the [Exit] button.#ref(WiX Toolset 2-1.png,80%,center)Installing Graphviz  Start the installer and click the [Next] button.#ref(Graphviz 1-1.png,60%,center)   Change the installation folder as desired, and click the [Next] button.#ref(Graphviz 2-1.png,60%,center)   Click the [Next] button to start installation.#ref(Graphviz 3-1.png,60%,center) #ref(Graphviz 4-1.png,60%,center)   After installation is complete, click the [Close] button.#ref(Graphviz 5-1.png,60%,center)   When installing from the msi, the path is not set automatically, so you need to add the path to the environment variables manually. Right-click Command Prompt and select [Run as administrator].  Enter and execute the following command in Command Prompt.＞setx /M PATH “%PATH%;[installation folder path]” #ref(Graphviz 6-1.png,80%,center)If it succeeds, “SUCCESS: Specified value was saved.” will be displayed.  Close Command Prompt once, and then open it again.   To confirm that each Graphviz command can be used, enter the following command. ＞dot -V#ref(Graphviz 7-1.png,80%,center) If the version is displayed, setup is complete.Linux EnvironmentThe packages required can be installed using the script used when installing OpenRTM-aist.      pkg_install_ubuntu.shpkg_install_debian.shpkg_install_fedora.shpkg_install_raspbian.sh    $ sudo sh pkg_install_***.sh -l c++ -l python -c --yes  Batch InstallationFor Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, and Raspbian, see the batch installation procedure here.Common Settings for Windows/LinuxInstaller Package NameFor Windows, the package name consists of “RTC project name + RTC version number_OpenRTM-aist version number_architecture”.The version number uses a format with dots removed; [1.0.0] becomes [100].For Linux, it consists of “RTC project name_RTC version number_architecture”.Example: package names when a package is created with the following settings  Project name: RobotController  Version number: 1.0.0      OpenRTM-aist version: 1.2.0    For Windows          32-bit: RobotController100_rtm120_win32.msi      64-bit: RobotController100_rtm120_win64.msi        For Ubuntu and Debian          32-bit: robotcontroller_1.0.0_i386.deb      64-bit: robotcontroller_1.0.0_amd64.deb        For Fedora          32-bit: RobotController-1.0.0-i686.rpm      64-bit: RobotController-1.0.0-x86_64.rpm      The “RTC version number” is the value specified on the “Basic” tab in RTCBuilder.RTC Version NumberSpecifying the Installation Destination DirectoryThe location where the created installer package is installed when executed is, by default, the OpenRTM-aist installation destination.Only in the Windows environment can the installation destination be changed as desired on the GUI screen when installing OpenRTM-aist.The default installation destination path is determined by the following conditions.  The path of OpenRTM-aist installed in the environment where the installer package was created  RTC language  The module category specified on the Basic tab when generating the RTC (default: Category)Any string can be entered for the module category.Setting the Module Category Name to "Controller"If this RTC is “C++” and the installer is created in an environment where the 32-bit version of OpenRTM-aist 1.2.0 is installed on Windows, the default installation destination is as follows. C:\Program Files (x86)\OpenRTM-aist\1.2.0\Components\C++\Category\RobotControllerIf a package is created in a Linux environment, the installation destination is as follows. This example uses “Controller” as the module category. /usr/share/openrtm-1.2/components/c++/Controller/RobotControllerPackage Maintainer InformationThe package maintainer information reflects the content entered in “Author / Contact” on the “Documentation Generation” tab in RTCBuilder.The format must be entered as “name ". The name must be written in Roman letters, and the email address must be enclosed in < >.If left blank, it becomes "unknown". (The default is blank.)#ref(Maintener 1-1.png,80%,center)

title: Update Method
content: #contentsThis section explains the procedure for updating OpenRTP (the collective name for RTCBuilder and RTSystemEditor). Since OpenRTP is provided as an Eclipse plugin, the operation is performed on Eclipse.Updating OpenRTPFrom the Eclipse menu, select [Help] > [Install New Software].Click the [Add] button in the “Install” dialog and add the repository. Specify the name and location as follows.  Name : OpenRTP  Location : http://openrtm.org/pub/openrtp/stable/updates/Check OpenRTP 1.1.0 and click the [Next] or [Finish] button.During installation, a screen asking whether to trust the certificate will open. Check the checkbox and click the [OK] button.After installation, restart as instructed, and the update will be applied.How to Apply the Update to Existing ComponentsFor projects of components that have already been generated, handle them using the following procedure, for example.  Load them into eclipse again and regenerate the code (delete the project once on eclipse, then import it again)  In the eclipse Package Explorer screen, double-click RTC.xml in the project and click the [Generate Code] button  At this time, a diff screen will be displayed, so update only idl/CMakeLists.txtOn Linux or Mac, simply replace it with sed. $ sed -ie 's/\"\${ALL_IDL_SRCS}\"/ALL_IDL_SRCS/' idl/CMakeLists.txt

title: Creating an rpm with CPack (Linux)

For a C++ RTC   $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー $ mkdir build $ cd build $ cmake .. $ make $ cpack  For a Pyrhon RTC $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー $ mkdir build $ cd build $ cmake .. $ cpackCreation Procedure When Including doxygen DocumentationChange the following line in CMakeLists.txt directly under the project directory from OFF to ON.For a C++ RTC, this is around line 86, and for a Python RTC, around line 77. option(BUILD_DOCUMENTATION "Build the documentation" ON) ※この行の OFF を ON に書き換えます。(デフォルトは OFF)  For a C++ RTC $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー $ mkdir build $ cd build $ cmake .. $ make $ make doc $ cpack  For a Pyrhon RTC $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー $ mkdir build $ cd build $ cmake .. $ make doc $ cpack[Notes]If you turn ON the documentation build and run “cpack” without running “make doc”, the following error will occur. CMake Error at /home/プロジェクトディレクトリー/build/doc/cmake_install.cmake:36 (file): file INSTALL cannot find "/home/プロジェクトディレクトリー/build/doc/html/doxygen/html".rpm Package Storage Location and File NameIf it is created successfully, it will be saved in [build] inside the project directory.The file name will be “RTC project name-RTC version number-architecture”.(Example) Flip-1.2.0-x86_64.rpm  The architecture will be [i686] or [x86_64].How to Check an rpm Package  When checking an rpm package with the less command $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー/build  $ less Flip-1.2.0-x86_64.rpm Name        : Flip Version     : 1.2.0 Release     : 1 Architecture: x86_64 Install Date: (not installed) Group       : unknown Size        : 506080 License     : unknown Signature   : (none) Source RPM  : Flip-1.2.0-1.src.rpm Build Date  : 2017年xx月xx日 xx時xx分x秒 Build Host  : localhost Relocations : /usr  Vendor      : AIST Summary     : Flip image component Description : DESCRIPTIONPress “q” to exit less.  When extracting and checking the contents of an rpm packageIf the tree command is not installed, install it. $ sudo apt-get install tree $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー/build  $ dpkg -x Flip-1.2.0-x86_64.rpm . $ tree usr usr └─ share    　└─ openrtm-1.2        　　└─ components            　　　└─ python               　　　 　└─ Category　※指定したインストール先ディレクトリー                    　　　　　└─ FlipGUI                        　　　　　　├─ RTC.xml                        　　　　　　├─ FlipGUIComp.py                        　　　　　　├─ idl                        　　　　　　│    ├─ BasicDataType.idl                        　　　　　　│    ├─ CMakeLists.txt                     　　　　　　   │    ├─ CalibrationService.idl                  　　　　　　      │    ├─ ExtendedDataTypes.idl                        　　　　　　│    └─ InterfaceDataTypes.idl                        　　　　　　├─ idlcompile.sh                      　　　　　　  ├─ rtutil.py                        　　　　　　├─ setup.py                        　　　　　　└─ flipgui.pyInstalling and Uninstalling an rpm PackageInstallationRun the following command to install. $ cd プロジェクトディレクトリー/build  $ sudo rpm -i Flip-1.2.0-x86_64.rpmUninstallationRun the following command to uninstall. $ sudo rpm -e FlipIDL Compilation Processing for Python RTCs with Service PortsPython RTCs with service ports execute IDL compilation when the package is installed.This behavior is implemented by postinst.in and prerm.in in the project directory during IDL compilation execution, so be careful not to delete these files, as the function will stop working.The following is a list of files installed from the rpm package. Files marked with ★ are generated by IDL compilation. $ tree /usr/share/openrtm-1.2/components/python/Category/FlipGUI/ /usr/share/openrtm-1.2/components/python/Category/FlipGUI/  ├─ BasicDataType_idl.py  ★  ├─ CalibrationService_idl.py  ★  ├─ ExtendedDataTypes_idl.py  ★  ├─ ImageCalibService  ★  │   └─ __init__.py  ★  ├─ ImageCalibService__POA  ★  │   └─ __init__.py  ★  ├─ InterfaceDataTypes_idl.py  ★  ├─ RTC  ★  │   └─ __init__.py  ★  ├─ RTC.xml  ├─ RTC__POA  ★  │   └─ __init__.py  ★  ├─ FlipGUIComp.py  ├─ idl  │   ├─ BasicDataType.idl  │   ├─ CMakeLists.txt  │   ├─ CalibrationService.idl  │   ├─ ExtendedDataTypes.idl  │   └─ InterfaceDataTypes.idl  ├─ idlcompile.sh  ├─ rtutil.py  ├─ setup.py  └─ flipgui.py

title: Installation and Startup
content: #contents(4)This section explains how to install and start RTCBuilder.Installing RTCBuilderSince RTCBuilder is an Eclipse plugin, you must first install Eclipse itself and the other Eclipse plugins on which it depends.For installation, please refer to Installing OpenRTM Eclipse tools.Starting RTCBuilderWhen you start Eclipse for the first time after installation, the following “Welcome” screen is displayed.Screen when Eclipse is started for the first timeClick the “X” button at the upper left of this “Welcome” screen, and the following page will be displayed.Click the [Open Perspective] button at the upper right, and select “Other” from the pull-down menu.Switching PerspectivesSelect “RTC Builder” and click the [OK] button.Selecting a PerspectiveRTCBuilder starts.Initial screen when RTCBuilder startsStarting the RTC Profile EditorTo open the RTC Profile Editor, click the [Open New RtcBuilder Editor] button on the toolbar, or select [File] > [Open New Builder Editor] from the menu bar.                  Open New RtcBuilder Editor from the Toolbar    Open New Builder Editor from the File Menu  Enter a project name in the displayed new project creation dialog.Creating a Project for RTCBuilder 1The code generated using RTCBuilder, RTCProfile, and other files are saved under the project created here.By default, the project is created under the workspace being used (inside the directory set in “Location”).If you want to create the project in any location, turn off the “Use default location” checkbox and specify the location in “Location”.A project with the specified name is generated and added to the Package Explorer.Creating a Project for RTCBuilder 2In the generated project, an RTC profile XML (RTC.xml) with default values is automatically generated.

title: Screen Layout and Functions (Build View)
content: #contentsThe Build View is a view for graphically displaying the configuration details of the RT component being created.An example of the Build View is shown below.Build ViewIn the Build View, the configured RT component name, the number and names of data ports (InPort/OutPort), the number and names of service ports, and the number and names of service interfaces are displayed.Each port is also displayed at the position specified in each configuration screen.Displaying the Build ViewIf the Build View is not displayed when switching to the “RTCBuilder” perspective, it can be displayed by following the steps below.From the menu at the top of the screen, select [Window] > [Show View] > [Other]. In the displayed “Show View” screen, select [OpenRTP Tools] > [BuildView].                  Displaying the Build View

title: Compilation Method (Windows, Java)
content: #contentsThis section explains how to build with Java.PreparationYou need to install Java Development Kit 6 in advance. (Note: It does not work with Java 1.5 (5.0).)Build Procedure from RTC Builder  On the RTC Profile Editor screen, open the [Language/Environment] tab and select [Java].  Open the [Basic] tab and click the [Generate Code] button to generate the code.  If a development environment plugin for the code generation target language is installed, the following confirmation message is displayed, so click [Yes]. Then, in the displayed dialog, select [Java (default)] and click the [OK] button.For the Java language, JDT (Java Development Tools) is included in Eclipse in advance.  The project information is displayed in the Package Explorer, but some information is not displayed, so select [File] > [Refresh] from the menu, or click the [F5] key in the Package Explorer to refresh the information.  Right-click the [build_module name.xml] file and select [Run] > [1 Ant Build].  The build is executed, and the build results are displayed on the console screen.  If an error is displayed on the console screen, check whether the JDK is installed correctly. From the menu, select [Window] > [Preferences] > [Installed JREs].Check whether the installed JDK is selected. If it is not displayed, add the installed JDK using the [Add] or [Search] button. References  A new Java project cannot be created as JDK6 (1.6) compliant  How do I set a classpath to an arbitrary folder and perform an Ant build?  An exception is displayed when building from the command line using Ant with JavaBuild Procedure from the Command Prompt  Download Apache Ant from the following site. Apache Ant is software for executing builds. Eclipse includes the Ant plugin by default, but you need to download it in order to execute builds from the command prompt.Download: the Apache Ant Website  Extract the Zip file and change the folder name as desired. (Example: apache-ant-x.xx.x → ant)  Move it to any folder. (Example: C:\Program Files\ant)  Set the environment variables. (The screen shown is from Windows 10.)  Open the System Properties screen and click the [Environment Variables] button.  Click the [New] button under “System variables”.  Enter “ANT_HOME” for the variable name and “C:\Program Files\ant” for the variable value, then click the [OK] button. * Specify the path to the ant folder as the variable value.  From the “System variables” list, select the variable name “Path” and click the [Edit] button.  Click the [New] button, enter “%ANT_HOME%\bin”, and click the [OK] button.  Set JAVA_HOME. This is not necessary if it is already set.Click the [New] button under “System variables”.  Enter “JAVA_HOME” for the variable name and “C:\Program Files\Java\jdkx.x.x.x_xxx” for the variable value, then click the [OK] button.          Specify the path to the Java installation folder as the variable value.        Return to the System Properties screen and click the [OK] button to close the screen.  Restart the PC.  After restarting, start the command prompt and enter “ant -version” to check the Apache Ant version.  Similarly, enter “java -version” to check the Java version. title: ROS Transport (rosport)
content: initCommunicating with ROS nodesThis is the announcement for ROS support in OpenRTM-aist. This page will shortly be replaced with a tutorial on using the ports.The patch can be downloaded here.The sample components can be downloaded here.Although I guess it’s not a common thing yet, there have been murmuringsfor quite a while now here in Japan about a desire to be able to useOpenRTM-aist and ROS together. We would gain the huge range offunctional software and the persistent channel-based communications ofROS, and keep the strong life-cycle and execution management ofOpenRTM-aist.So here’s a patch for OpenRTM-aist that does exactly that.This patch adds a new transport type to OpenRTM-aist specifically forcommunicating across ROS channels. No doubt someone will find theability to use a persistent channel for communication useful, but themain benefit is that it gives nearly-seamless communications betweencomponents written for OpenRTM-aist and nodes written for ROS. Yournetwork of distributed components/nodes no longer has to be in just oneframework.There are no wrappers involved. It’s all native communication using thesame ROS libraries as you would use in a pure-ROS system - notranslation layers means maximum efficiency. You create a port type forthe ROS transport, and off you go. If you already know ROS, you’ll feelright at home using the ports.The one caveat is why I say nearly-seamless: we still don’t have aunified set of types (also, there are some issues with the typing systemin OpenRTM-aist that we’re working to sort out). Fortunately, the typesissue is a hot topic amongst framework designers at the moment, so Ihope we will have solved that problem before too long.I have attached both the patch, for OpenRTM-aist-1.0.0, and a set ofexamples for each port type (publisher/subscriber/client/server). I hopeto get a web page up on the OpenRTM-aist site shortly with a moredetailed explanation of usage; for now, the examples and the doxygencomments in the source will point you in the right direction - it’s allpretty simple.Comments, suggestions, and improvements are welcome.

title: Creating RT Components (Java Version)
content: init#contentsOverviewOpenRTM-aist-Java OverviewOpenRTM-aist is an implementation of RT middleware implemented, distributed, and maintained by the Task Intelligence Research Group, Intelligent Systems Research Institute, National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology. RT middleware and OpenRTM-aist are software platforms that make it possible to build various robot systems by dividing the various functional elements of robots into component units called RT components and freely combining them. They also conform to The Robotic Technology Component Specification, a middleware specification for robots currently being standardized by the OMG (Object Management Group). OpenRTM-aist-Java is a port of OpenRTM-aist, which has been provided for the C++ language, to the Java language. It has an interface compatible with the C++ version of OpenRTM-aist, and enables interoperability between RT components developed using the Java language and RT components developed using the C++ language.Target AudienceThis document explains how to develop Java-language RT components using OpenRTM-aist-Java. This document assumes that readers already have basic knowledge of the Java language.Operating EnvironmentThe environment required to run OpenRTM-aist-Java is as follows.Table 1-1 Operating Environment      Environment    Remarks        Java Development Kit 5.0 (JDK 5) (http://java.sun.com/products/archive/j2se/5.0_14/index.html )    Note: It does not work with Java 1.4.  For details on how to install OpenRTM-aist-Java, refer to the “OpenRTM-aist-Java Installation Manual (UNIX)” or the “OpenRTM-aist-Java Installation Manual (Windows)”. In particular, check the following before proceeding with the work below.  The version displayed when executing “java -version” matches the JDK above  The path (base path) to the OpenRTM-aist-Java library is set in the environment variable RTM_JAVA_ROOT            The library files OpenRTM-aist-0.4.x.jar and commons-cli-1.1.jar exist in the directory “jar” directly under the path set by  (to set them as the classpath) **Note**                                                  Note It is also possible to set your own classpath by referring to this page .                                          ◆Reference:   JDK 5 installation method (UNIX) ,  JDK 5 installation method (Windows)    How to set system environment variables (UNIX),  How to set system environment variables (Windows)   FAQ: Support for FedoraCore when installing Java   FAQ: How can I set a classpath to any folder and perform an Ant build? &aname(javacomp);About Developing Java RT ComponentsHere, we introduce the procedure for developing Java RT components. As a sample, we will use a component with the following specifications.Table 2-1 Sample Component Specifications      Basic Profile        Component name    sample        Description    SampleComponent        Version    1.0        Vendor    AIST        Category    example        Component type    DataFlowComponent        Activity type    SPORADIC        Maximum number of instances    5        Data InPort        Name    in        Type    TimedLong        Service Provider        IDL path    IDLs/MyService.idl  Note        Port name    MySvcPort        Service name    myservice0        Service type    MyService        Configuration Parameter        Name    multiply        Type    int        Default value    1  Note Create the following IDL file, MyService.idl, using an appropriate editor. Also, describe the path to MyService.idl in the “IDL path” in the table above. In Windows, this “IDL path” must be the full path to MyService.idl. typedef sequence<string> EchoList; typedef sequence<float> ValueList; interface MyService {   string echo(in string msg);   EchoList get_echo_history();   void set_value(in float value);   float get_value();   ValueList get_value_history(); };MyService.idlThe above MyService.idl is identical to the one in the “examples/Java/RTMExamples/SimpleService” directory of the samples included with OpenRTM-aist-0.4-Java.Procedure for Developing RT Components Using the GUIThis section explains the procedure for developing RT components using RtcTemlate, a GUI tool. For details on RtcTemplate, refer to Installing RtcLink and RtcTemplate and RtcTemplate.Integration of RtcTemplate and JDT  Open Eclipse as “New”RT components can also be developed from projects in the Eclipse integrated development environment. Specify a new workspace and click the [OK] button. Eclipse starts. (At this time, a “Welcome” screen may be displayed; close it.)Figure 2-2 Specifying a new Workspace  Creating a Java Project FileSelect [File] > [New] > [Project] from the top menu.Figure 2-3 Creating a build project 1In the “New Project” wizard, select “Java Project” and click the [Next] button.|Figure 2-4 Creating a build project 2In the next step of the “New Project” wizard, enter the “Project name” to be created. Confirm that the setting in the “JDK Compliance” group is “5.0” or higher (or 1.5 or higher), and then click the [Next] button (Figure 2-5). On the other hand, depending on the environment, the “JDK Compliance” frame may be a “JRE” frame, and JDK5 (or JDK1.5) may not be selectable from the pull-down menu (Figure 2-5’). In that case, refer to this page  to make it possible to select the JDK.|Figure 2-5 Creating a build project 3Figure 2-5' Depending on the environment, the JDK may not be selectable  Reference:          → FAQ: Q. A new Java project cannot be created as JDK5 (1.5) compliant |                  In the displayed “New Java Project” screen, configure various settings for the project to be generated and click the [Finish] button.      Figure 2-6 Complete after configuring various project settings            The specified project is generated and displayed in the “Package Explorer View”.      Figure 2-7 Example display in the Package Explorer view  Disable automatic buildIf [Project] > [Build Automatically] in the Eclipse menu bar is turned on, it is better to clear the check and disable it.Note For details about Eclipse, such as options and settings when creating a project, refer to the Eclipse site and other resources.Generating Skeleton Code Using RtcTemplate  Starting the GUI RtcTemplate EditorStart the RtcTemplate editor screen.  Reference:          → Starting RtcTemplate directlyNote For information on how to use RtcTemplate, refer to RtcTemplate.        Editing settings in the RtcTemplate editorThe settings for generating skeleton code for an RT component with the specifications shown in Table 2-1>#javacomp using the GUI version of RtcTemplate are shown below.Figure 2-8 GUI RtcTemplate settingsNote: In Windows, describe the above “Output directory” and “IDL path:” as full paths.
